last_seen.description:
When the book last CONFIRMED this rung, as an ISO timestamp, whether or not
its price moved. Pinnacle realtime only (`getRealtime` and `pinnacle-realtime`);
absent on `/odds` and on feeds that do not stamp rungs.

Pinnacle does not resend every rung in every message, so a rung whose
`last_seen` is well behind its market's `last_seen` is a hint that the rung has
been taken down, not proof. Rungs are never flagged `suspended` one by one.

awayTeamId.description: Stable roster id for `awayTeam`; same rules.

commenceTime.description:
Scheduled start of the game. Cut `recordedAtUtc` (not the stored `recordedAt`) against this to separate
pre-game odds from in-play ones exactly, rather than by date.

Absent whenever the start time was not captured: every game archived
before 2026-09-20, and any game since whose start we could not resolve.
Treat its absence as "unknown", never as a start of midnight.

gameDate.description: The DATE the game is filed under, which is a UTC date and not the start time.

homeScore.description: Final score, absent when the archive did not capture one.

homeTeamId.description:
Stable roster id for `homeTeam`, absent when the name is not on a roster
we carry. Note the casing: camelCase here, `home_team_id` on `/odds`.

periodScores.description:
Per-period scores, absent when none were captured. `period` is a label,
not an index: `"Q1"`..`"Q4"` then `"OT1"`, `"OT2"` for the quarter sports
(nba, wnba, nfl, ncaaf), and the plain period or inning number for
everything else. A bare `"OT"` is never sent.

propsSnapshots.description: Stored props rows for the eventId; `null` when not counted (as oddsSnapshots).

source.description: How the row got here: the live pipeline, or a backfill run.

BallybetV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Bally Bet v2 events (`ballybet-v2-update`).
The same 25 sports as {@link BetriversV2BookSubscription}. Use `'*'` for a
whole sport or exact league keys from
{@link OwlsInsightRest.getBallyBetV2Leagues }; Bally Bet's price boosts are
under `specials` (e.g. `{ specials: ['nfl-boosts'] }`).

BaseballScoreDetail.description:
Baseball-specific live detail.

`inning`/`half` are present for live games only. `hits`/`errors` complete the
R-H-E line — runs are `home.score`/`away.score`, and per-inning runs are
`home.linescores`/`away.linescores`.

Outs and runners on base are NOT available: the upstream source does not
carry them.

half.description: Half of the current inning. Live games only. Absent when the source does not say.

pitcher.description: Pitcher the source currently lists for each side.

BasketballPlayDetail.description: NBA: the action sub type, the player, the shot.

Bet105V2BookSubscription.description: Per-sport league filter for `v2: { bet105: {...} }`. Any Bet105 sport.

Bet365V2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Bet365 v2 events.

Bet365 v2 supports both multi-league sports (soccer, requires
specific league keys) and single-league sports (nba, mlb, nhl, nfl, where
the entire sport is one stream). For single-league sports pass `'*'`;
arrays are accepted and coerced to `'*'` server-side.

soccer.description: League filter for soccer. Discover keys via {@link OwlsInsightRest.getBet365V2Leagues }.

BetMGMGameProps.description: BetMGM game props — flat props[] instead of books[] wrapper.

BetMGMPlayerProp.description: BetMGM-specific player prop (flat structure, no over/under pairing).

BetOnlineV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for BetOnline v2 events (`betonline-realtime`).

Every sport takes a {@link V2LeagueFilter}, and every sport on this book is
competition-keyed — there is no single-league sport here. So unlike bet365,
mybookie and thunderpick, an array filter is NOT coerced to `'*'`
server-side: BetOnline is deliberately excluded from that coercion list,
because its rooms really are per-competition and coercing would hand you a
blend of competitions you did not ask for. An array is a real filter, and a
key that matches no competition simply receives nothing.

Use `'*'` to take the whole sport (all competitions), or list exact league
keys from {@link OwlsInsightRest.getBetOnlineV2Leagues } — passing the sport
name as a league key (e.g. `{ mlb: ['mlb'] }`) is not a wildcard and will
miss Liga Mexicana, MiLB and anything else the sport carries.

BetusV2BookSubscription.description: Per-sport league filter for `v2: { betus: {...} }`. Any BetUS sport.

BookStatusData.description: Per-book data freshness status sent with odds-update payloads.

event_link.description: Deep link to event page on sportsbook website (REST only, stripped from WebSocket).

total.description: Total matching rows, or null when no filters applied (for performance).

oneXBetSoccer.description:
Opt-in to the isolated 1xBet SOCCER feed (`1xbet-update` events). Default:
not subscribed. 1xBet soccer is NOT in /odds — it's a scrape-based feed on
its own channel. (1xBet esports is unaffected and stays in the odds stream.)

plays.description:
Play-by-play subscription (`plays-update`) as the server kept it: `true`, or the
valid play-by-play sports you sent. Absent when nothing valid was sent.

prophetx.description: ProphetX exchange subscription (opt-in — default: undefined/no events).

realtime.description: Realtime feed opt-out; present only as `{ ps3838: false }`.

scores.description: Live scores subscription (`scores-update`; opt-in, default: undefined/no events).

v2.description: Source API (v2) subscription (opt-in — default: undefined/no events).

v2Advisory.description:
Set by the server, never sent: what happened to each per-league v2 filter you
sent (accepted but unverified, dropped, or widened to `'*'`). League keys are
not checked at subscribe time, so read this when a v2 subscription stays silent.

v2OptionsAdvisory.description:
Set by the server, never sent: what happened to the book-level v2 options
(`v2.polymarket.eventTypes` and `marketTypes`), including an event type that
this connection will not receive.

ClosingOddsDataQuality.description:
Per-response data quality for /history/closing-odds.

This endpoint never withholds rows. A price that cannot be a valid American odd
(|price| < 100, which indicates a decimal coefficient stored in an integer
column) is omitted per FIELD, leaving the row and its other markets intact.

rowsExcluded.description: Always 0 — rows are never excluded by this endpoint.

suppressedFields.description: Count of individual price fields nulled across this response.

lastUpdate.description: Epoch SECONDS from the source. The column is BIGINT UNSIGNED, so this is a number.

moneyline.description:
`draw` is present ONLY for three-way sports (soccer). Two-outcome sports omit
the key entirely rather than sending `draw: null`, so `Object.keys(moneyline)`
is safe and an MLB row never advertises an outcome that does not exist.

For soccer, computing implied probability from home+away alone will NOT
reconcile — you must include the draw.

source.description: Provenance. Several sources can coexist for the same (event, book).

spread.description:
Every field null means the spread was captured but withheld: on a live-derived
close, a spread whose two points do not cancel or one known to be wrong for that
book and date (counted in `dataQuality.suppressedFields`). Absent means none was captured.

line.description:
The totals line. Null only when the whole total was withheld (a live-derived
close known to be wrong for that book and date); the prices are then null too.
The API omits `total` when none was captured.

ClosingOddsSource.description:
Where a closing-odds row came from. These are NOT interchangeable:
 - `football-data`  the bookmaker's FINAL published closing price
 - `live-derived`   the last snapshot our own capture saw, which is only as
                    close to the close as capture ran that day
 - `yahoo`/`oddsshark`/`espn`  the original third-party backfill (MLB + NBA)
For closing-line-value work prefer `football-data` where present.

ConnectErrorCode.description:
Why the server refused a connection, in `err.data.code` on `connect_error`. More
codes can be added.

Not retryable (reconnecting with the same key cannot succeed until something
changes on your account): `MISSING_API_KEY`, `INVALID_API_KEY`,
`API_KEY_DEACTIVATED`, `TIER_NO_WS`, `SUBSCRIPTION_INACTIVE`, `PAYMENT_OVERDUE`,
`TRIAL_EXPIRED`, `TRIAL_UNVERIFIABLE`.

Retryable: `SUBSCRIPTION_CHECK_FAILED`, `INTERNAL`, `IP_BLOCKED`,
`CONNECTION_LIMIT` (every connection your plan allows is in use), `CLIENT_CLOSED`.

ConnectErrorData.description: `err.data` on a `connect_error` the server refused. Absent from API versions that predate it.

maxConnections.description: On `CONNECTION_LIMIT`: how many connections your plan allows.

retryAfterMs.description: Wait at least this long before trying again.

retryable.description: True when reconnecting later with the same key can succeed.

event_types.description: One or more event types. A type that is not open yet is refused with a 400 (`event_type_unavailable`).

url.description: https on the default port with a public hostname. IP addresses and private or internal hosts are refused.

DayScheduleBuildWindow.description: The days the schedule is built for: three UTC days back to nine ahead.

DayScheduleCompetitor.description:
One side of a game. Team sports list away then home; tennis and UFC list the
first then the second competitor, with `side` null.

score.description: Null before the game has a score.

sets.description: Tennis only: games won in each set, in set order.

winPrice.description:
Kalshi price to buy this side to win, 0 to 1, so the two sides can add to a
little over 1. Null once the market closes, and null when the market is too thin
to price.

winner.description: Set once the game is final; null before then, and on a level final score.

DayScheduleGame.description: One game on the day schedule.

competition.description: Tennis tournament or UFC event name; null elsewhere.

competitors.description: Always two entries; see {@link DayScheduleCompetitor} for the order.

drawPrice.description: Soccer only: Kalshi price for the draw.

eventId.description: The game's eventId on /api/v1/{sport}/odds when it was found there, else null.

id.description: Stable for the life of the game, even when it is rescheduled.

liveUpdatedAt.description: When this game's live data (status, score, clock) was last read; null before it has any.

round.description: Tennis round, playoff "Game N", or UFC weight class; null when none.

volume.description: Kalshi volume across the game's winner markets, in contracts. Games starting together are ordered by it.

DayScheduleMeta.description:
Freshness of a day-schedule answer. `status`, first match wins:
- `no-data`: nothing built for the range.
- `stale`: built more than 3 minutes ago, the schedule not refreshed for 5
  minutes, or live scores more than 90 seconds old while a game has started and
  not finished.
- `partial`: the range reaches outside `buildWindow`, a day in range was not
  built, or the list behind the build was cut short.
- `ok`.

cacheTimestamp.description: Build time of the least recently built day in range; null when none is known.

liveAgeSeconds.description: Seconds since live data (scores, clocks) was last read in full.

source.description: Where the schedule comes from, currently "kalshi".

window.description: The UTC range served: local midnight of `date` to local midnight `days` later.

DayScheduleResponse.description:
Response from GET /api/v1/schedule. `games` are in start order (larger volume first
among games starting together).

date.description: The day asked for (or today in `tz`), YYYY-MM-DD.

sports.description: The sports asked for (every sport by default).

DayScheduleStartCheck.description: The game's start time compared with independent sources.

differsByMinutes.description: The larger of the two gaps below, in minutes; null when neither differs.

flashscoreMinutes.description: Minutes between this start and the scores feed's start, when they differ.

sportsbooksMinutes.description: Minutes between this start and the sportsbooks' start, when they differ.

DayScheduleStartCheckResult.description: How an independent source's start time compares with the schedule's.

DayScheduleStatus.description:
A game's state on the day schedule. Open: a new value must not break a reader.
- `unconfirmed`: the scheduled start passed long ago and no live data confirms the
  game started or ended, or live data for a game in progress stopped updating for
  more than 10 minutes.
- `time_tbd`: the start time is not set yet.

DraftKingsV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for DraftKings v2 events.

Each key is a sport `draftkings-v2-update` carries. Soccer and mma are multi-league
(filter by league keys, or `'*'` for all); the others are one league each (pass
`'*'`). Soccer, mma and wnba push their markets as they change. nba, nhl, mlb, nfl,
ncaab and ncaaf push only the live slice (marketId `live`), unless it is too large
to send; their main catalog is REST only. Unknown / unsupported sport keys are
rejected at compile time.

mlb.description: Single league: pass `'*'`. Pushes only the live slice (marketId `live`); the main catalog is REST only.

mma.description: League filter for MMA: `ufc` (UFC bouts), or `'*'`.

nba.description: Single league: pass `'*'`. Pushes only the live slice (marketId `live`); the main catalog is REST only.

ncaab.description: Single league: pass `'*'`. Pushes only the live slice (marketId `live`); the main catalog is REST only.

ncaaf.description: Single league: pass `'*'`. Pushes only the live slice (marketId `live`); the main catalog is REST only.

nfl.description: Single league: pass `'*'`. Pushes only the live slice (marketId `live`); the main catalog is REST only.

nhl.description: Single league: pass `'*'`. Pushes only the live slice (marketId `live`); the main catalog is REST only.

soccer.description: League filter for soccer. Discover keys via {@link OwlsInsightRest.getDraftKingsV2Leagues }.

EVBoard.description: The board an EV response was read from, and how old it is.

ageMs.description: Age of the board when this response was sent, in milliseconds; null when there is no board.

builtAt.description: When the board was built (ISO 8601); null when there is no board.

stale.description: True when there is no board or it is too old: no EV is served from it.

venueQuotes.description: Whether the board holds Kalshi or Polymarket quotes.

venues.description: Whether this request asked for Kalshi and Polymarket (`venues=true`).

EVEvent.description: A game with its fair and the +EV opportunities found across books.

booksInConsensus.description: Independent price sources behind the event's fair.

canonicalEventId.description: Our stable id of the game, `{sport}:{away}@{home}-{date}`: the `eventId` the odds board and the history endpoints use. Null when unknown.

eventId.description: The game's `id` on the odds board. The history endpoints take `canonicalEventId` instead.

fair.description: How the fair was formed, and the fair per side before the margin.

fairProbability.description: The conservative fair per side (the fair minus 1 percentage point); null for a side with no fair. The fair before the margin is in `fair`.

EVFair.description:
How an event's fair was formed, and the fair per side before the 1-point margin.
Each side is de-vigged on its own, conservatively, so the sides can sum to slightly
less than 1.

anchor.description: Which Pinnacle line anchored the fair: the realtime feed or the /odds entry; null when Pinnacle did not.

away.description: Fair probability of an away win before the margin; null when there is none.

draw.description: Fair probability of a draw before the margin (three-way markets); null otherwise.

home.description: Fair probability of a home win before the margin; null when there is none.

method.description:
`pinnacle`: Pinnacle's de-vigged line. `consensus`: no Pinnacle line, so the median
of at least three independent books; only venues are scored against it, never a
sportsbook. Null when there is no fair (`reason` says why).

reason.description: Why there is no fair, in plain text; null when there is one.

sources.description: Independent price sources behind the event's fair.

EVLineEvent.description: One game and market with its +EV prices.

fair.description: The fair per side before the margin, and how it was formed (always Pinnacle on spreads and totals).

fairProbability.description: The conservative fair per side, keyed home/away (spreads) or over/under (totals).

point.description: Pinnacle's main number: the home side's number on spreads, the total on totals.

pushPossible.description: A whole number: a push refunds the stake. The fair is each side's chance given no push.

EVLineMarket.description: A spread/total market: `spreads` (sides home/away) or `totals` (sides over/under).

EVLineOpportunity.description: One +EV price on a spread or total, scored at Pinnacle's main number. Same math as {@link EVOpportunity}.

booksInConsensus.description: Independent sources behind the fair this price was scored against (1 = Pinnacle alone).

evPct.description: On a whole number, the EV of a bet that is not refunded by a push.

fairProbability.description: The conservative fair (the fair minus 1 percentage point); evPct, edgePp, kellyFraction and fairPrice are computed at it.

point.description: This side's own number: -3.5 on the favourite, +3.5 on the underdog; the total on totals.

team.description: Team name on spreads; "Over" or "Under" on totals.

line.description: Every price is compared at Pinnacle's main number only.

market.description: The markets asked for, e.g. "spreads" or "spreads,totals".

unsupported.description: Set when the sport's books do not agree on what a handicap counts (tennis, esports, MMA): no line is scored.

EVOpportunity.description:
One +EV opportunity: a sportsbook price, or a venue's ask (an exchange such as Novig,
and with `venues: true` the prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket), that beats the
fair.

The fair is Pinnacle's de-vigged line: the other books do not move it, they only
veto a side they disagree with (when Pinnacle has no line, a venue can be scored
against a consensus of books instead; see `EVFair.method`). `fairProbability` is the
CONSERVATIVE fair, the fair minus 1 percentage point, and `fairPrice`, `evPct`,
`edgePp` and `kellyFraction` are all computed at it. The fair before that margin is
`fairUnadjusted`.

book.description: Sportsbook or venue key. `kalshi` and `polymarket` are listed only with `venues: true`.

bookImplied.description: Implied probability of `bookPrice` (a sportsbook's includes its vig; a venue's is its ask).

bookPrice.description: American odds of the price: a sportsbook's price, or a venue's ask.

booksInConsensus.description:
Independent price sources behind the fair this price was scored against. A
sportsbook's own feed never counts toward its own fair, so 1 means Pinnacle alone.

evPct.description:
Expected value %, at `fairProbability`. Sportsbook: `(fairProbability * decimalOdds - 1) * 100`.
Venue, its fee included: `(fairProbability - ask - fee) / (ask + fee) * 100`.

fairProbability.description: The conservative fair probability of this outcome: the fair minus 1 percentage point. `fairPrice`, `evPct`, `edgePp` and `kellyFraction` are computed at it.

fairUnadjusted.description: The fair probability before the 1-point margin: `fairProbability` is this minus 0.01.

fee.description: The venue's trading fee per contract, in dollars; 0 for a sportsbook.

kind.description: `book` for a sportsbook, `venue` for an exchange or prediction market (Novig, Kalshi, Polymarket).

link.description: The market's page at the venue; null for a sportsbook.

quoteAgeMs.description: Age of the price when this answer was served, in milliseconds, by its own timestamp; null when unknown.

reason.description: Why it is not tradeable, in plain text (such as `EV under 2%`); null when it is.

roi.description: `evPct / 100`, not rounded: EV per dollar staked (sportsbook) or per dollar paid, fee included (venue).

route.description: Kalshi and Polymarket: the contract to buy, `yes`, or `no:<CODE>` (NO on the opponent's market). Null otherwise.

size.description: Dollars available at the ask; null when unknown (Polymarket, sportsbooks).

tradeable.description:
Whether the opportunity clears the markets page trade bar. Sportsbook: EV of at
least 2%. Venue: EV of at least 4%, a bid, a spread of 4 cents or less and at least
$50 at the ask.

EVResponse.description:
Response for `GET /api/v1/{sport}/ev` (MVP+). Pre-game value bets only.

No opportunity is listed while the odds snapshot behind the answer is over 90
seconds old, or for a game that has started. Within that, a sportsbook price must be
under 3 minutes old and an exchange quote (Novig by default, Kalshi and Polymarket
with `venues: true`) under 2 minutes, each by its own timestamp.

The optional fields (`kind`, `fairUnadjusted`, `roi`, `fee`, `tradeable`, `reason`,
`route`, `size`, `link` and `quoteAgeMs` on an opportunity, `canonicalEventId` and
`fair` on an event, `board` in `meta`) come with `fair_method: "fair_v1"`.

board.description: The board the response was read from. Sent with `fair_method: "fair_v1"`.

fair_method.description: How the fair is computed: `fair_v1` (Pinnacle's de-vigged line, the other books only veto, a 1-point margin). `consensus_devig_median` is the method it replaced.

freshness.description: Age of the odds snapshot behind the answer. `ageSeconds` is always a number; `stale` is true when the snapshot is over 90 seconds old or there is no data.

timestamp.description: When the odds snapshot behind the answer was written (ISO 8601); `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` when there is no data at all.

EsportsRealtimeMeta.description: Per-event meta on the esports realtime REST response.

EsportsRealtimePayload.description:
Pinnacle esports realtime payload for a single game. Delivered via
{@link OwlsInsightEvents} as `cs2-realtime`, `lol-realtime`,
`valorant-realtime`, or `dota2-realtime`.

**Pinnacle wire format** — no team-name normalization, prices in
American odds. The `events` array carries Pinnacle matchups directly
(`participants`, `markets[].prices[].designation/price/points`,
`markets[].limits[]`).

EsportsRealtimeResponse.description:
Response shape for `GET /api/v1/{cs2|lol|valorant|dota2}/realtime?league=...`.

**Distinct from `RealtimeResponse`** — the traditional `getRealtime(sport)`
call returns normalized `OddsEvent[]` for nba/nhl/etc. The esports realtime
endpoints return the Pinnacle wire format (matchups with `participants`,
`markets`, `prices`, `limits` — no team normalization, prices in American
odds). Each item in `data` is shaped like one `EsportsRealtimePayload.events[i]`.

EsportsRealtimeSubscription.description:
Per-game subscription filter for the Pinnacle esports realtime
WebSocket events ({@link OwlsInsightEvents}).

Each entry MUST include a `league` substring — the server never broadcasts
the firehose unfiltered. Mirrors the REST `/api/v1/{game}/realtime?league=`
required query param.

EventFreshness.description:
Per-event freshness on the realtime streams. Keyed off PRICE MOVEMENT
(`lastUpdate`), not feed re-confirmation (`refreshedAt`), so a frozen-but-still-
served live line reads `stale: true` — the market-maker pull signal.

ageSeconds.description: Seconds since the price last moved — tradeability age.

lastUpdate.description: Epoch ms this event's price last MOVED (drives `stale`/`ageSeconds`), or null.

refreshedAgeSeconds.description: Seconds since the feed last confirmed this row.

refreshedAt.description: Epoch ms the feed last CONFIRMED this row (moved or not) — liveness, not movement.

stale.description: Live row whose price has not moved within the stale window — not tradeable.

EventPhase.description:
{@link OddsEvent.phase}. More values can be added: treat an unknown one like a
missing field.

away_team_id.description: Stable roster id for `away_team`; same rules.

eventId.description: Formatted event ID for use with history endpoints.

home_team_id.description:
Stable roster id for `home_team`, absent when the name is not on a roster
we carry. Same values as {@link OddsEvent.home_team_id}.

available_leagues.description:
Every league value present for this sport, before any `league` filter.

Use it to discover valid `league` values instead of guessing them, and to
tell a filter that matched nothing from a genuinely empty slate: a
non-empty `available_leagues` with `event_count: 0` means the filter missed.

league.description: The `league` filter that was applied, echoed back.

FairEvent.description: A game's fair line. A market is null when there is no current fair for it.

method.description: `pinnacle`, or `consensus` (at least three independent books) when Pinnacle has no line.

american.description: Its American odds: the break-even price.

booksDisagree.description: The other books' median fair chance differs from Pinnacle's by more than 1.5 percentage points on this side.

probability.description: The fair (no-vig) chance of this side.

FairPrice.description: One side of a fair price.

american.description: Its American odds: the break-even price.

booksDisagree.description: The other books' median fair chance differs from Pinnacle's by more than 1.5 percentage points on this side.

probability.description: The fair (no-vig) chance of this side.

FairResponse.description: Response for `GET /api/v1/{sport}/fair` (MVP+): the Owls fair line.

markets.description: Which markets this sport is priced on.

FanDuelStateMarketIdsMeta.description: meta.fanduelMarketIds (getProps) / meta.marketIds (getBookProps fanduel) when `state` was sent.

mapped.description: marketIds (props and alternate-line rungs) rewritten to the state's id.

timestamp.description: When the state map was last refreshed.

unmapped.description: FanDuel marketIds with no id for the state, omitted rather than served as New Jersey's.

FanDuelStateOddsMeta.description: meta.fanduelMarketIds on getOdds (and the per-market routes) with `state`.

available.description: false: no FanDuel ids for this sport and state, every FanDuel marketId omitted.

mapped.description: FanDuel outcomes whose marketId is the state's.

timestamp.description: When the state's ids were last refreshed; null when `available` is false.

unmapped.description: FanDuel outcomes with no id for the state, marketId omitted.

FanDuelV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for FanDuel v2 events.

Each key is a sport FanDuel v2 currently supports. Soccer, tennis and mma
are multi-league: filter by specific league keys or `'*'` for all.

mlb.description:
Single-league sports: pass '*'. FanDuel v2 measurably pushes deltas for these
(observed mlb 77 and nfl 38 events in a 100s window), and the server accepts
any VALID_SPORTS key here, so omitting them made real subscriptions untypeable.

mma.description: League filter for MMA: `ufc` (UFC bouts), or `'*'`.

soccer.description: League filter for soccer. Discover keys via {@link OwlsInsightRest.getFanDuelV2Leagues }.

tennis.description: League filter for tennis. Discover keys via {@link OwlsInsightRest.getFanDuelV2Leagues }.

FanaticsMarketsV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Fanatics Markets v2 events.
Use `'*'` for a whole sport or exact series keys (e.g. `['mls']`) from
{@link OwlsInsightRest.getFanaticsMarketsV2Leagues }.

books.description:
Also receive the live order books of the sports above on
`fanaticsmarkets-books-v2-update` (within about a second of a move).
Off by default: `fanaticsmarkets-v2-update` carries the events alone.

FootballPlayDetail.description: NFL and NCAAF: the down and distance before (`down`…) and after (`endDown`…) the play.

data.description: Differs between the response shapes; untyped.

meta.description: Differs between the response shapes; untyped.

HardRockLadderEntry.description: One rung of the Hard Rock price ladder.

americanOdds.description: Decoded American odds for this rootIdx.

rootIdx.description: Hard Rock's price-ladder index, as it appears on each selection.

even.description: rootIdx for EVEN money (+100). Below = favorites, above = underdogs.

ladder.description: Verified rootIdx → American-odds anchors, ascending by rootIdx.

decoding.description: Human-readable description of the exact-lookup + interpolation rule.

sports.description:
Keyed by sport. A sport that is absent usually has no rows in this dataset,
which is a distinct case from an empty range, but it is also absent when its
lookup failed; such a partial answer is not cached, so ask again later before
concluding a sport is not covered.

HistoryCoverageRange.description: First and last date actually held for one sport in one historical dataset.

HistoryOddsDataQuality.description:
What `/history/odds` says about the rows it just returned. Both flags are
always `true`; they exist so the accompanying notes have somewhere to hang.

mainLineOnly.description: Each row is one book's main line for that market and side.

suspectPricesExcluded.description: Unusable rows (a destroyed price, or no market label) are excluded.

dataQuality.description: What these rows are and what was left out of them.

meta.description:
`archive` when a completed game was served from the history archive store,
`live` when read from the database. The payload shape is identical either
way. Note this one object mixes casings: `source` and `archiveBuiltAt` are
camelCase, the ignored report is snake_case, and that is the wire.

ignored_params.description: Query parameters the endpoint did not honour, sorted. Absent when none were.

ignored_reasons.description: Why, keyed by parameter name; only for entries that have a reason.

statType.description: Stat type discriminator. null = BasketballStats, "batter"|"team_batting" = BattingStats, "pitcher"|"team_pitching" = PitchingStats.

point.description: The stored line, which may arrive as a decimal string such as `"-1.50"`.

timestampUtc.description: `timestamp` in UTC, or `null` when its clock cannot be known; `timestamp` is the stored time (US Eastern for many rows stored before 2026-09-16). Added Oct 2026.

HistoryPropsDataQuality.description: Present on /history/props when any row on the page is flagged: counts per flag and what each means.

HistorySplitsResponse.description: Response for GET /api/v1/history/splits. Rows are oldest first.

eventId.description: Echoed when the request named an eventId.

sport.description: Echoed when the request named a sport.

window.description: The UTC date window served (both ends inclusive), on a query by sport only.

HockeyPlayDetail.description: NHL: the players involved by role, the ice position, the shot or penalty.

homeShotsOnGoal.description: On shots: the shots on goal after this one.

situationCode.description: The league's skaters-and-goalies code for the situation on the ice.

HockeyPlayer.description: One player on an NHL play: `role` is scorer, assist, shooter, goalie, winner, loser, hitter, hittee, blocker, player, committedBy, drawnBy or servedBy.

name.description: Null when the league's roster for the game does not list the id.

conflicts.description: Players both sources cover but disagree about. Counted over what is SERVED.

listDaysConflicts.description: Players both sources call injured but disagree about the LENGTH of.

reportAgeSummary.description:
Freshness of THIS response. The first four partition the players returned
and sum to `count`; the last three describe how much of the whole response
could be dated and are not scoped to those buckets.

InjuryAgreement.description: Whether the sources corroborate one another for this player.

InjuryConsensus.description:
Derived agreement between sources. Present ONLY when the player's identity is
certain; absent players are listed in `meta.unresolvedIdentity`.

idVerified.description: True only when a shared player id corroborates the name-and-team join.

injuryStatus.description: Null on a conflict: an indeterminate answer is its own verdict, never a pick.

listDaysConflict.description:
True when both sources agree a player is on an injured list but disagree
about its length, for example 10 days against 60. `agreement` still reads
"agrees", so check this when the length matters.

stale.description:
Whether the designation is still current, judged against `staleAfterSeconds`.

True when every dated record behind it is older than the window, false when
at least one is inside it, and null when no verdict is possible. Null is
never a substitute for false.

staleAfterSeconds.description:
The window the designation was judged against, in seconds, chosen by what the
designation IS rather than by sport alone: a weekly football designation
lapses far sooner than a baseball injured-list stint, which is given its own
length plus grace.

Read it together with `stale` to tell the two nulls apart. A number beside a
null `stale` means the rule exists but nothing carried a timestamp. A null
here means no rule applies at all.

suffixJoin.description: True when the join bridged a name suffix. Disclosed rather than hidden.

records.description: Every source's own view, always present, never collapsed.

reportAge.description: How much of this player's evidence could be dated, and how old it is.

InjuryReportAge.description: How much of a player's evidence carries a timestamp, and how old it is.

newestSeconds.description: Age of the most recently dated record. Null when nothing is dated.

oldestSeconds.description: Age of the least recently dated record. Null when nothing is dated.

InjurySourceLabel.description:
Which of the sport's sources a record came from.

Deliberately a ROLE, not a vendor name: "primary" is the source the API leads
with for that sport. The label stays correct if a source is swapped underneath
it, and it is stable across sports, where the primary differs.

ageSeconds.description:
Seconds since this source was last stored, or null when unknown. Never 0 as a
stand-in for unknown.

checks.description: The validations that ran on THIS source's data. Never pooled across sources.

lastDataAgeSeconds.description: How long since this source last produced a non-empty result.

lastFetchError.description: The reason CODE of the last refused write. Free-text detail is not served.

metaMismatch.description:
Present when the stored metadata did not describe the stored data, so its age
and counts were not trusted and `ageSeconds` is null. Surfaced rather than
quietly corrected, because the divergence is itself the signal.

InjurySourceRecord.description: One player's status according to ONE source. Never merged with another source's view.

bodyPart.description: A factual descriptor such as "Ankle", not editorial copy.

listDays.description: Injured-list length in days, where the source encodes one.

playerName.description: This source's own spelling of the name, which is why it can differ per record.

reportAgeSeconds.description:
Seconds since this source published the state, derived from `reportedAt`.

Null when the source publishes no timestamp, and never 0 as a stand-in for
unknown. Distinct from `meta.sources[source].ageSeconds`, which is how long
ago the feed was fetched: a designation weeks past its weekly reissue can sit
behind a fetch that happened seconds ago.

reportedAt.description:
The SOURCE's timestamp for this state, not when it was fetched. Null when the
source publishes none.

statusLabel.description: The source's own display string, verbatim. Shown, never compared.

teamId.description: Canonical team id, stable across sources and sports.

InjuryStatus.description:
Normalised availability. `unmapped` is a first-class value, not an error: an
unrecognised upstream token surfaces as unknown rather than defaulting to
healthy, because "healthy" is an affirmative claim you would act on.

InjuryUnresolvedIdentity.description: Why a player could not be given a consensus.

KalshiV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Kalshi v2 events.

Each Kalshi sport carries one or more series (game lines, props,
futures). Pass `'*'` to receive every series for that sport, or an
array of Kalshi series tickers / league slugs to filter.

wnba.description: Added for the 2026 season; both are live on this book's v2 REST + WS.

category.description: Source's own market category (e.g. "Team Props", "Game Props").

description.description: Source's own market description, where the book provides one.

isAlternate.description: True when this entry is an alternate line rather than the main line.

key.description:
Market identifier.

On the Pinnacle `/realtime` pipeline, markets folded from a sub-matchup are
keyed `special_<matchupId>_<type>_p<period>`. ALTERNATE ladders additionally
carry their LINE, because a key that resolves to several markets does not
identify one:
  `special_1634192207_total_p0_alt_10.5`
  `special_1634192207_spread_p0_alt_-3`   <-- CAN BE NEGATIVE
A spread's line is stated from the home side, so `_alt_` may be followed by
a minus sign; do not assume that segment parses as an unsigned number.
Non-alternate keys (`special_<id>_total_p0`) and team-total keys
(`special_<id>_team_total_p0_home_1.5`) are unchanged.

A rung whose line MOVES changes key — a different line is a different rung.
If you map markets by key, key each rung separately; keying only on the
family collapses a ladder onto whichever rung you saw last.

last_seen.description:
When the book last CONFIRMED this market, as an ISO timestamp, whether or not
the price moved. Pinnacle realtime markets only.

Use this, not `last_update`, to judge whether a quote is still live: a quiet
line the book keeps re-confirming has a fresh `last_seen` and an old
`last_update`, so `last_update` alone cannot tell a quiet line from a pulled one.

Compare a line against ITS OWN history, not against other lines on the same
game. Lines on one match are confirmed at very different rates (the main line
far more often than alternates or period lines), so a line that trails its
siblings is normal. A line whose `last_seen` stops advancing when it normally
keeps moving has stopped being quoted.

last_update.description: When this market's price last CHANGED. It does not move when the book re-confirms an unchanged price.

side.description:
The source's own market-level side designation, passed through unmodified.

Set on markets that price ONE competitor rather than both. The case it
exists for is a team total, whose outcomes are named only `over` / `under`,
so nothing inside the market says whose total is priced.

Join it yourself: `side === 'home'` means the event's `home_team`,
`side === 'away'` means its `away_team`. The API deliberately does not
resolve the name, because the resolved string came from a different naming
layer than `home_team` / `away_team` and failed to join.

Set today only by the Pinnacle `/realtime` pipeline, on `special_*` markets.

suspended.description:
True when betting on this market is closed: the book closed it, and on the
Pinnacle realtime feed it can also be set once the market's period is closed or
its betting cutoff has passed. Absent otherwise, never `false`.

On the Pinnacle realtime feed it is also set on a main market (moneyline,
spread, total or team total) that Pinnacle withdraws while the rest of the match
stays open, and cleared when Pinnacle offers it again or its period ends. On a
spread or total only the main line is flagged, never its `alternateLines`.

Its absence does NOT mean every line is being quoted: a withdrawn alternate rung,
or a special or prop market, can arrive with no `suspended` at all. Use
`last_seen` (on the market, and on each rung) to tell whether a quote is live.

units.description:
The source's own unit-of-measure for the sub-matchup this market came from,
passed through unmodified.

NOT AN ENUM — match it exactly and treat unknown values as unknown. Values
seen in one soccer sample: `Regular`, `Corners`, `1st Goal`, `2nd Goal`,
`CombinedResult`, `Place 1st`. Tennis team totals report `Games`. It varies
by sport AND by market, so do not hard-code a whitelist you expect to be
exhaustive.

Matters most on `special_*` team totals: one soccer event can carry a goals
team total AND a corners team total folded on from different sub-matchups,
and `units` is what separates them. Absent means the source stated no unit;
do NOT read absence as "goals".

MarketStructure.description:
Market structure as published by the upstream sportsbook. Tells the consumer
how to interpret `line`, `overPrice`, and `underPrice` together. Populated
from upstream signals — not inferred client-side.

- `over_under`: Both Over and Under selections published with a continuous
  line (e.g. strikeouts 5.5). Standard interpretation.
- `milestone`: Upstream provides an explicit threshold count (e.g. DK's
  `milestoneValue: 1` = "1+ of category"). `line` is the threshold value
  verbatim. `underPrice` is always null.
- `single_sided`: Only one side published (typically Over for rare-event
  props). The missing side is `null`, not inferred.
- `pick_one`: Multi-selection market where each selection is one
  participant's Yes price (e.g. anytime touchdown scorer).

ABSENT DOES NOT MEAN `over_under`. Treat a missing value as UNKNOWN; see
{@link PlayerProp.marketStructure} for why defaulting it is a settlement bug.

lastUpdated.description: Last time the score or state changed.

score.description: Null for a scheduled match (never a 0-0). Soccer: excludes shootout goals.

MyBookieV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for MyBookie v2 events.

MyBookie is single-league per sport (mlb, nba) — pass `'*'`. Arrays
are accepted and coerced to `'*'` server-side (V2_SINGLE_LEAGUE_PAIRS).

simplified.description: Simplified form (noise words stripped, lowercased). Only for soccer/tennis.

away_team_id.description: Stable identifier for the team behind `away_team`; same rules as `home_team_id`.

freshness.description:
Per-event freshness on the realtime streams (`/{sport}/realtime` +
`pinnacle-realtime` WS). `freshness.stale` flips true when THIS event's price
has not MOVED within the stale window (default 30s) even if the feed keeps
re-confirming it — the honest per-line signal a market-maker keys a "pull my
quote" decision on (vs the coarse sport-level `meta.freshness`). Sent on
`pinnacle-realtime` and on `/{sport}/realtime` responses whose `meta.source` is
`"pinnacle"`. Absent on `/odds`; do not rely on it on the PS3838 feeds.

home_team_id.description:
Stable identifier for the team behind `home_team`, e.g. `"la-lakers"`.
The same team carries the same id across every book and every spelling of
the name, so you can join on it instead of on the string.

The key is ABSENT (never `null`) when the name is not on a roster we carry:
every tennis competitor, soccer and college names outside our rosters, and
outright events, which never carry ids at all.

isLive.description:
In-play flag on the realtime feeds.

When `phase` is present: true while a live line for the match is started and
not ended, meaning in-play betting on it is running.

Without `phase`: the book's own flag for its live-betting offering, which does
not mean "in play" and can be false on a match in progress, so check `status`
as well.

`freshness.stale` applies to an event that reads as in play.

lastUpdate.description: Epoch ms of the newest price change on this event (realtime only).

market_type.description:
`'outright'` for aggregated futures/progression markets (e.g. Pinnacle
"To Reach The Final") that are NOT team-vs-team games. For these, the single
`bookmakers[].markets[].outcomes` list holds the competitors (each with a
price), `home_team` carries the market label, and `away_team` is empty.
Absent for real games. Currently surfaced on the realtime (`/realtime`,
`pinnacle-realtime`) soccer feed.

phase.description:
Where the event is in its life, from Pinnacle's own live-line fields. Pinnacle
realtime only: `/{sport}/realtime`, `pinnacle-realtime`, and `ps3838-realtime`
events that carry it. Absent everywhere else.

- `scheduled`: not started.
- `live`: in play, betting open.
- `suspended`: in play, betting paused for now.
- `closed`: betting over for good. The event is sent this way for a few
  minutes, then removed.

This list can gain values. Treat a value you do not recognise like a missing
field, and read `phase` before `isLive` or `status` whenever it is present.

seenAt.description: Epoch ms the feed last CONFIRMED a price on this event, changed or not (realtime only).

droppedAsFinished.description: Events dropped because the match was confirmed finished (realtime only).

droppedAsStale.description:
Events dropped because their scheduled start is older than the sport's
max plausible live duration — a source-independent staleness guard
(realtime only).

dataQuality.description:
Which snapshots were withheld as unusable. `allPricesSuppressed` (with its own
`note`) means the market has recorded history but every snapshot in it was withheld.

mainLineOnly.description: Each row is one book's main line for that market and side.

suspectPricesExcluded.description: Unusable rows (a destroyed price, or no market label) are excluded.

point.description:
Same column, same query and same type as `history[].point`: the stored
line, which may arrive as a decimal string such as `"-1.50"`.

timestampUtc.description: `timestamp` in UTC, or `null` when its clock cannot be known; `timestamp` is the stored time (US Eastern for many rows stored before 2026-09-16). Added Oct 2026.

available_leagues.description: Every league key on the sport's board, so a `league` value can be checked.

exchangeBooks.description: The prediction-market exchanges this board can carry (kalshi, polymarket, novig).

excludeExchanges.description: Echo of `excludeExchanges`: true when the exchanges were left out.

fanduelMarketIds.description: Present when `state` was sent: the FanDuel marketId rewrite. Added Oct 2026.

ignored_params.description:
Query parameters the endpoint did NOT honour, sorted. Present only when
something was ignored, so a clean request carries no key at all (never an
empty array). A name we do not read, or a filter whose value did not
resolve, lands here instead of silently returning the full board.

ignored_reasons.description:
Why a name in `ignored_params` was ignored, keyed by that name. Present
only for the entries that have a reason: an unknown parameter name has
none, so it appears in `ignored_params` alone.

inPlay.description:
Whether the game was in play when the row was captured.

Three states, and the third is an ABSENT KEY: `true` in play, `false`
pre-game, absent when the phase was not recorded. Absent covers every row
written before 2026-09-20, every esports row, and rows from sources that
do not derive a phase. Do NOT read a missing key as `false`: that files
unknown-phase rows as pre-game.

point.description:
The line (spread or total) as stored: a decimal string such as "-1.50",
because the archive keeps two-decimal precision as text. Prefer
`pointValue`, which is the same line already parsed. null for moneylines.

pointValue.description:
`point` as a number, always present: `-1.5` beside `"-1.50"`. `null` when
the line is null or could not be parsed, and never `0` for either, so
`null` and a genuine zero line stay distinguishable.

price.description:
American odds (integer). For decimal-native books (e.g. 1xBet) this is the
American conversion; see `priceDecimal` for the exact upstream value.

priceDecimal.description:
Exact upstream decimal (European) odds at full precision, e.g. 1xBet 2.387.
Populated for decimal-native books; null for American-native books.
Available on snapshots archived after the price-precision fix (2026-07).

recordedAtUtc.description:
The capture time in UTC (ISO, ends in Z), or `null` when its clock cannot be known (rows stored
before 2026-03-28, and book `pinnacle` before 2026-04-10). `recordedAt` is the time as stored: most
rows stored before 2026-09-16 hold US Eastern wall time even though the value ends in Z. Use this
one for time arithmetic. Added Oct 2026: absent on an API older than that.

OddsUpdatePayload.description:
Payload for `odds-update` WebSocket events.

Frames can be partial. After a subscribe the first frames are a snapshot of the
sports and books you asked for; later frames carry only the games that changed.
Merge each event into your own state by `id` instead of replacing your state with
a frame.

sports.description: Odds keyed by sport (e.g. "nba", "nhl"). Each sport contains OddsEvent[] with bookmakers nested inside; merge them by `id`.

OneXBetSoccerResponse.description:
Response for `GET /api/v1/1xbet/soccer` — the isolated 1xBet SOCCER feed.
1xBet soccer is intentionally NOT in `/odds` (it's a scrape-based, best-effort
fresh feed). 1xBet *esports* is unaffected and remains in the normal streams.

OneXBetSoccerUpdate.description: Payload for the WebSocket `1xbet-update` event (isolated 1xBet soccer).

OpeningLineData.description: Opening line snapshot sent with odds-update payloads.

deepLink.description:
Ready-made URL that opens this outcome on the sportsbook, pre-built with a
host that resolves the ids. Optional and absent for most books — read it
defensively rather than assuming every outcome has one.

What the link does differs by book. Read this before putting one behind a
button labelled "add to betslip":

- **FanDuel** — `nj.sportsbook.fanduel.com/addToBetslip`, adds the selection
  to the existing slip. The NJ host is required, not cosmetic: the
  underlying `marketId` namespace only resolves on that subdomain. For
  another state, request `state` (getOdds, getProps): `marketId` is then
  that state's and `deepLink` is left out; the `selectionId` is the same
  in every state.
- **DraftKings** — `sportsbook.draftkings.com/event/{eventId}?outcomes=...`,
  which opens the event with the outcome selected. Not region-locked at the
  ID level; DraftKings applies its own state gating once the slip opens.
- **Hard Rock** — `share.hardrock.bet/Pt0T/landing?deep_link_value=…`, Hard
  Rock's AppsFlyer share host. On a phone with the app installed it opens
  the app on the selection; without the app it goes to the app store, and
  there is no mobile web fallback. On desktop the `af_web_dp` parameter is
  reported to send the visitor to `app.hardrock.bet` (inherited claim, not
  verified by us).
  **This one REPLACES the betslip.** Hard Rock's handler clears the existing
  slip before it resolves and adds the selection, so anything the customer
  had already built is discarded. Label it accordingly. A logged-out visitor
  is prompted to sign in and the selection lands after they do.
- **Novig** — `novig.onelink.me/JHQQ?…&deep_link_value=…`, an AppsFlyer
  OneLink that PREFILLS a slip with this one side (no stake prescribed).
  Hands off to the Novig app when installed; there is no web autofill
  fallback. Novig is an exchange, so the price quoted is a peer's resting
  order — treat the click as an order to place, not a guaranteed fill.
  Only the props form of this link has been click-tested; game-line links
  come off the same builder but have not been.

Books not listed here do not publish a link today.

liquidity.description:
Order-book depth, on exchanges that expose a book (Novig today).

⚠️ `size` is in CENTS, the exchange's native unit — NOT dollars and not
contracts. `size: 47691` is **$476.91**. Divide by 100 before showing it
to anyone or sizing a bet against it; reading it as dollars overstates
available depth by 100x.

⚠️ `price` here is AMERICAN ODDS, converted from Novig's native
probability so this surface matches every other book in `/odds`. The
player-props feed does NOT do this — `PlayerProp.liquidity` levels carry
`price` as a raw probability (0–1) and size as `qty`/`qtyDollars`. Do not
share a parsing path between the two.

Levels are best price first, up to a 100-level safety bound (server-side,
`NOVIG_LIQUIDITY_DEPTH`). Deepest observed to date is 57, so nothing is
clipped today, but there is no flag telling you a ladder WAS clipped.
Main markets were capped at 5 levels until 2026-08-21; player props never
were, which is the asymmetry a customer reported.

`asks` is empty in practice on Novig — its ladders are bids-only (measured
across 2,659 outcomes), so an empty `asks` is the venue, not missing data.

Attached to the PRIMARY line only, not to alternate lines. A deep ladder's
tail can hold real but far-out-of-the-money resting orders (observed up to
+99900 at ~0.1% implied) — read the tail as depth, not as "the price".

Absent for traditional sportsbooks and for exchange outcomes with no ladder.

asks.description: Always present, but empty on Novig — its ladders are bids-only.

bids.description: Best bid first. `price` = American odds, `size` = CENTS.

marketId.description:
The sportsbook's own market identifier for the parent market, passed through
verbatim. Use it to correlate an outcome with the book's public API, not to
hand-build a link — `deepLink` is the supported way to link out.

Present only when the book publishes one. Do not assume a book that carries
`deepLink` also carries a usable `marketId`: Hard Rock's link format resolves
a selection on its own and never consults a market id.

selectionId.description:
The sportsbook's own identifier for this specific outcome, passed through
verbatim.

The type is book-dependent — FanDuel publishes a number (`29172`),
DraftKings a string (`'0ML85877697_3'`). Compare loosely or coerce; do not
assume one or the other.

A `selectionId` with no `deepLink` beside it means the id did not match a
shape we could safely put into that book's URL, so no link was emitted.
Treat the id as a correlation key in that case, not as link material.

PinnacleRealtimeSyncPayload.description:
Payload of the `pinnacle-realtime-sync` event: a stream position, removals, or both,
for a sport that has no events to send. It never carries events. Sent on the same
connections and for the same sports as `pinnacle-realtime`; track `stream` and
delete the `removed` ids exactly as you do there. See {@link RealtimeOddsPayload}.

feed.description: The sport's upstream feed state ({@link RealtimeFrameFeed}).

removed.description: Event ids to delete from your board, keyed by sport.

PinnacleV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Pinnacle v2 events.

Single-league sports (wnba, nba, mlb, nhl, ncaab, ncaaf, nfl) map 1:1
to a sport key — pass `'*'` to receive every matchup, or an array
containing the same sport key (filters are tolerated for forward
compatibility).

Multi-league sports (tennis, soccer, esports, handball, mma) use slugified
Pinnacle league names as filter values (e.g. `'atp-singles'`).

Play.description:
One play of an NBA, NHL, NFL, NCAAF or soccer game, as GET /{sport}/plays and the
`plays-update` event carry it. Merge plays by `id`: a play can be amended after it
is first published (a review, an assist added). For soccer a play is a match
incident (goal, card, substitution), not every pass.

clock.description: Time left in the period as the venue shows it ("5:32"), or for soccer the match minute ("67", "45+2"); null when the source has none.

id.description: The source's play id, unique within the game.

secondsRemaining.description: Null for soccer, whose clock counts up.

seq.description: The source's own order within the game: ascending, not contiguous.

team.description: The side the play belongs to (the offense, the shooter's team, the team that took the penalty, the side credited with a goal); null for a neutral play.

type.description: The source's own type key, unchanged: "Rush", "Pass Reception"; "shot-on-goal", "faceoff"; "2pt/Jump Shot", "rebound/defensive"; soccer "Goal", "Yellow Card", "Substitution".

updatedAt.description: When this version of the play was first seen: an amendment after first publication moves it.

wallclock.description: When the play happened according to the source; null for the NHL and soccer, which publish none.

averages.description: L5/L10/L20 rolling windows (computed by Owls Insight)

seasonAverages.description: ESPN's pre-computed season averages (label → value, e.g. "PTS" → "17.6")

seasonTotals.description: ESPN's pre-computed season totals (label → value, e.g. "PTS" → "704")

categoryRaw.description:
The raw upstream stat/unit string, present ONLY when `category` is `'unknown'`.
Lets you identify a market we have not mapped yet without re-deriving it from
the sportsbook, and tell an unmapped market apart from a genuinely
uncategorisable one. Added Jul 2026.

comboType.description:
Multi-player markets (`category: 'combos'`, Oct 2026): the market kind. `combined` prices the
players' total, `either` prices "either player reaches the line"; `other` for anything else.
The market itself is named in `playerName` as `"<players> - <market>"` (e.g.
`"Charlie McAvoy & JJ Peterka - Either Player Shots on Goal"`), so two markets for one pair never
share a name. A same-name twin in one game carries a stable `" (market <id>)"` suffix.

line.description:
Threshold value as published by the upstream sportsbook. Interpretation
depends on `marketStructure`. As of the DraftKings mapper passthrough
change (May 2026), DK's `milestoneValue` is no longer rebased to the
"industry-standard 0.5" — it is passed through verbatim. Consumers
that previously assumed `line === 0.5` for "1+" markets should read
`marketStructure` and treat `milestone` markets as "Nth+ where N = line".

liquidity.description:
Exchange liquidity. A UNION across books — which fields are present depends
on which book produced the prop:

* Kalshi — `volume`, `volume24h`, `openInterest`, `bidSize`, `askSize`
  (contracts).
* Polymarket — `amount`, `volume` (USD).
* Novig — `volume` plus the two order books below.

⚠️ Novig's `overBook`/`underBook` levels are NOT shaped like
`Outcome.liquidity` on the main-markets feed. Here `price` is a raw
implied probability (0–1) and size is `qty` (CENTS) with a `qtyDollars`
convenience already computed. There, `price` is American odds and size is
`size` (also cents, no companion field). Same venue, two surfaces, two
shapes — the props side is deliberate raw pass-through.

overBook.description:
Resting orders on the OVER side of this prop (Novig only).

⚠️ To TAKE the displayed OVER you look in `underBook.bids` at
`1 - overProbability`, not here — this book holds orders that would
MAKE the over. Getting this backwards reads the wrong side of the
market.

underBook.description: Resting orders on the UNDER side (Novig only). See `overBook`.

marketStructure.description:
How the upstream sportsbook structured this market. See {@link MarketStructure}.

ABSENT DOES NOT MEAN `over_under` — treat a missing value as UNKNOWN. On an
INTEGER line "over 20" and "20+" disagree at exactly 20, so defaulting to
over/under turns an unknown into a confident wrong settlement. (This doc
previously said to treat absence as `over_under`; that was wrong and is
corrected here.) Our own grading refuses to settle an integer line whose
structure is unknown, for the same reason.

overPrice.description:
American odds for the over.

On EXCHANGE books (currently `kalshi`) this is the venue's own ASK — the price a
buyer actually pays — as of Sep 2026. It previously carried the bid/ask MIDPOINT,
which nobody can trade at: measured across 40 live kalshi markets the published
number beat the takeable one on 40 of 40, median 3.5c and worst case 48c quoted
against 94c payable, so cross-book comparisons showed edges that had no
counterparty. Read {@link overPriceBasis} / {@link underPriceBasis} to see which
side each price came from.

overPriceBasis.description:
Which side of the book {@link overPrice} came from. Set only by exchange books,
where the distinction is real:

* `takeable` — the venue's ask: transactable now.
* `midpoint` — no ask was resting, so this is the bid/ask midpoint. An estimate of
  fair value, NOT a quote.

Absent on traditional sportsbooks, whose posted price is takeable by construction.

overPriceMid.description:
Bid/ask MIDPOINT as American odds, for books publishing a two-sided quote. The
better input to a no-vig fair line; {@link overPrice} is what you transact at.
Equal to `overPrice` exactly when {@link overPriceBasis} is `midpoint`.

players.description: Multi-player markets: the players the market prices, in the book's order.

rawMarketName.description: Multi-player markets: the book's own market name, verbatim.

underPriceBasis.description:
Under-side counterpart of {@link overPriceBasis}. SEPARATE on purpose: a book can
hold a resting ask on one side and not the other, so a single flag derived from
the over side would label a midpoint under-price `takeable` — a midpoint passed
off as a quote, under the one field meant to prevent that.

PlaysGame.description: One game in the list GET /{sport}/plays returns without an eventId.

PlaysGamesResponse.description: Response from GET /{sport}/plays without an eventId: the games that have play-by-play.

eventId.description: The event id as `getScores()` names the game.

lastSeq.description: The last play's seq; pass it as `since` to poll for new plays. Null when the game has no plays yet.

amendedWindowSeconds.description: With `since`: plays amended within this many seconds are included whatever their seq.

sourceAgeSeconds.description: The source's own edge-cache age at that read (NHL about 19 s, ESPN about 7 s); null when it sends none (NBA, soccer).

status.description: `stale` when a game in play has not been read for 30 seconds (soccer: 60).

PlaysSport.description: Sports served by GET /{sport}/plays and the `plays-update` event.

PlaysUpdate.description:
Payload of the `plays-update` WebSocket event: play-by-play for ONE sport.

Opt in with `subscribe({ ..., plays: true })` (nba, nhl, nfl, ncaaf and soccer) or
`plays: ['nfl', 'nba', 'soccer']`; no `plays` field, no messages. Same access as `scores-update`.
There is no full message: call `getPlays(sport, eventId)` once to start, then apply
each delta by merging `plays` by `id`.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 time the message was built.

PlaysUpdateEvent.description: One game on the `plays-update` event: the plays new or amended since the previous message.

count.description: Plays in the game after this message.

state.description: `post` once more when the game ends.

PolymarketV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Polymarket v2 events.

Each Polymarket sport is segmented by Polymarket tag slug (e.g.
`epl`, `ucl`, `nba`, `mlb`). Pass `'*'` for every tag, or an array
of tag slugs to filter.

eventTypes.description:
Which upstream message types to receive. Omit it for the default set: `book`,
`best_bid_ask`, `last_trade_price` and `tick_size_change`. List types to narrow
or extend it (`market_resolved` is only sent when you ask for it, by name or with
`'*'`), or pass `'*'` for every type available to your key. Omitted and `'*'` also
deliver upstream message types not named in {@link PolymarketV2EventType}; a list
delivers exactly the types it names. The `subscribed` acknowledgement reports
dropped values and any type this connection will not receive in
`v2OptionsAdvisory`.

These options apply to the polymarket sports listed next to them.
`updateSubscription` replaces the whole `v2` object, so send the sport keys again
together with the options.

marketTypes.description:
Only markets of these types (the `sportsMarketType` values on the REST
`data[*].markets[]`, for example `moneyline`). `'*'` or omitted means every type.
Values are not checked at subscribe time: one that no market carries never
matches, and the acknowledgement says so in `v2OptionsAdvisory`.

wnba.description: Added for the 2026 season; both are live on this book's v2 REST + WS.

PropOrderBook.description: One side of a Novig player-prop order book.

asks.description: Present but empty in practice — Novig ladders are bids-only.

PropOrderBookLevel.description:
One resting order in a Novig player-prop book, passed through verbatim.

Unlike `Outcome.liquidity` levels on the main-markets feed, `price` is an
implied PROBABILITY (0–1), not American odds.

originalQty.description: Originally posted size, before partial fills. Native unit (cents).

price.description: Implied probability of the outcome at this level (0–1).

qty.description: Size in the exchange's native unit — Novig posts CENTS.

actual.description: The measured stat. Null unless `status` is `ok`.

final.description:
Box scores are revised for a short window after a game. `false` means the row is
still provisional and may change.

playerId.description: Stable provider player id. Two players CAN share a display name.

ungradableReason.description: Why this entry could not be graded at all, independent of any book line.

capturePhase.description:
`commence` — captured on the pre-game to in-play transition. The real closing
line, and the only phase valid for closing-line value.

`archive` — captured at game end because the transition was missed. For a game
that ran live this is the LAST IN-PLAY price, a different thing entirely: an
in-play total in the eighth inning is nearly settled. Never pool the two.

marketStructure.description: How the book structured this market, when it published one. NULL means UNKNOWN.

PropResultsDayGame.description: One graded game listed by `getPropResults({ date })`.

gamesTruncated.description: True when the day's list hit its cap (NCAAB Saturdays can).

absentCategoryGroups.description:
Line groups for a player who IS in the box score but has no row for that
category. Expected for football — a quoted receiver with zero catches is in no
receiving group, so nothing is graded (never a 0, never a void). Kept apart from
`unmatchedLineGroups` so a real join failure is not buried in this benign count.

ambiguousPlayers.description:
Players refused as `ambiguous_player`, with every spelling seen and which side
of the join proved it. `from: "lines"` with spellings differing only by a suffix
is the disclosed trade-off: from names alone that could be two people.

checks.description: What was actually evaluated to produce this response.

entryStatuses.description:
Status counts, ONE PER PLAYER-CATEGORY ENTRY — including entries no book quoted,
which contribute nothing to `lineOutcomes`. Use these for "how many players did
not play", never the line counts.

lineOutcomes.description:
Verdict counts, ONE PER BOOK LINE. `over + under + push` is a LINE count, so a
rate built from it is weighted by how many books quoted each player.

nameVariantJoins.description:
Line groups joined to a box-score player written with another form of his first
name ("Alexandre Sarr" in the books, "Alex Sarr" in the box score): joined, and
disclosed like `suffixGaps`. NBA only; [] elsewhere.

provisional.description: Entries returned that are still provisional. OVERLAPS `entryStatuses`.

suffixGaps.description:
Joins that bridged a suffix — box score says "X Jr.", books say "X". Joined as
one player, usually rightly; disclosed because it is also the shape of the one
collision no name rule can see.

unmatchedLineExamples.description: A few of those, named, so the mismatch can be chased.

unmatchedLineGroups.description:
Closing-line groups no actual matched — a book quoted a player the box score did
not resolve under that spelling. Non-zero means the name join is losing data,
which otherwise looks exactly like "no book quoted this player".

unsupportedCategoryExamples.description: A few of those, named ("<player or roster> <category>"). NBA only; [] elsewhere.

unsupportedCategoryGroups.description:
Line groups in a category no box score grades (multi-player `combos`, award and
team markets): never a join failure, so not counted in `unmatchedLineGroups`.
Filled for NBA only; 0 for other sports, where those groups stay in the counters
above. Absent from responses of API versions before it was added.

closing.description:
Present with `line: "closing"`: every rung the book had captured at game start
(commence captures only — an archive row is an in-play line, never a close). The
game-level `verdict` comes from the rung with `isMain: true`; alternates are the
ladder and never decide. With no main rung the game is `no_closing_line`; with
more than one (rare) it is `multiple_closing_lines`.

decided.description: The hit-rate denominator. Excludes pushes AND unresolved games.

overRate.description:
overs / decided. NULL when nothing resolved — zero decided games is not a 0% hit
rate, so do not render a null as "0%".

streak.description: Consecutive run from the most recent game. Stops at the first unresolved game.

closingPhase.description: With `line: "closing"`: always `"commence"` — archive captures are excluded.

closingTruncated.description: With `line: "closing"`: true if the rung fetch hit its cap; games past the cut read as no_closing_line, so re-query with a smaller window.

gamesAvailable.description: Rows the lookback could see. A FLOOR when `gamesAvailableCapped` is true.

matchedNames.description:
The stored spelling(s) the returned games came from. MORE THAN ONE means the name
matched two distinct spellings that normalize identically — check them before
trusting the aggregate, because it may pool two different people.

provisional.description: Games in the lookback still marked provisional.

PropUngradableReason.description: Why a prop could not be graded. Never a verdict — always a stated reason.

PropbuilderV2BookSubscription.description: Per-sport filter for `v2: { propbuilder: {...} }`. Every sport is one league: pass `'*'`.

ProphetXCompetitor.description:
Competitor inside a ProphetX event. Stable fields — the server-side
publisher always emits these five keys for every competitor.

`seq` indicates home/away: 0 = home, 1 = away.

ProphetXDeltaPayload.description:
Payload for the WebSocket `prophetx-update` event.

Each delta contains ONLY the events (and within them, only the markets)
that changed since the previous publish. Clients should accumulate deltas
into their own state to maintain a full snapshot — or re-fetch the REST
endpoint for the current full state.

markets.description: Changed markets only, keyed by `"{market_id}:{line}"`. See {@link ProphetXMarket}.

sport.description: Raw ProphetX sport name — e.g. `Basketball`, `Ice Hockey`, `Golf`.

sportSlug.description: Slugified sport name matching the channel partition.

ProphetXEventData.description:
One event inside a ProphetX REST response.

The `event` field uses the stable `ProphetXRawEvent` shape (id, name, sport,
tournament, competitors, scheduled, status) with an index signature for any
extra ProphetX fields. The `markets` field is a keyed map of raw
ProphetX market payloads, typed as {@link ProphetXMarket}: the fields every
entry carries are required, the ones that depend on which envelope ProphetX
sent are optional, and everything else passes through the index signature.

lastUpdate.description: ISO timestamp of the last ingest for this event.

markets.description: Keyed by `"{market_id}:{line}"`. See {@link ProphetXMarket} for the shape.

ProphetXMarket.description: One `markets` entry: ProphetX's own market payload, verbatim.

favouriteMarketLine.description:
ProphetX's market-favourite line. FREQUENTLY NOT THIS KEY'S LINE: measured
2026-09-02, 531 of 1,321 entries carrying it quoted a different line than
the key (same id, different `line` and prices). Never read prices from it;
the book for this key is `selections` / `marketLines[0]` only.

line.description: The line this entry is keyed on; 0 for moneylines.

outcomes.description:
Absent on delta-shaped entries, where the labels sit under
`marketLines[0].outcomes` instead — {@link prophetxOutcomes } resolves it.

selections.description:
Sides, each levels-best-first or null. NULL AT THE TOP LEVEL on
delta-shaped spread/total entries — read `marketLines[0].selections`
then, or call {@link prophetxBook }.

totalStake.description: ProphetX market-level aggregate (catalog-shaped entries). Not executable liquidity.

traded_value.description: ProphetX market-level aggregate (delta-shaped entries). Not executable liquidity.

ProphetXMarketLine.description: One line of a spread/total market as ProphetX groups it.

selections.description: Sides, each an array of levels (best first) or null when empty.

exchange.description: Always `true` for ProphetX — indicates this is a betting exchange, not a traditional book.

requestedSports.description: Echo of the sports that matched the filter (slug form).

ProphetXOutcome.description: One outcome of a ProphetX market. `outcomes[i]` pairs with `selections[i]`.

outcome_link.description: Bet-slip deep link, synthesized by the API when ProphetX gives it the ids.

ProphetXRawEvent.description:
Raw ProphetX event metadata. The stable top-level fields are typed
(id, name, sport, tournament, competitors, etc.) while ProphetX's other
extension fields pass through via the index signature. Matches the shape
of `ProphetXEvent` in the nba-odds-app source of truth.

ProphetXSelectionLevel.description: One resting price level on one side of a ProphetX market.

id.description: Outcome id — equals `outcomes[i].id` for the side this level sits in.

line.description: Spread or total for this level; 0 on moneylines.

lineID.description: ProphetX line id; also used by `outcome_link`.

stake.description:
The resting order's stake as ProphetX reports it. Equals what `value`
wins on an untouched order, but stays at the original figure after a
partial fill — derive payout from `value` and `odds`, not from this.

value.description: Amount available for YOU to bet at this price right now, in dollars.

sports.description: Keyed by raw ProphetX sport name — e.g. `Basketball`, `Ice Hockey`, `Golf`.

totalEvents.description: Total number of events across all sports in the response.

ProphetXSportSlug.description: Valid ProphetX sport slugs accepted by REST filter and WS subscription.

ProphetXSubscription.description:
ProphetX WebSocket subscription filter.

  - omitted / false    → do NOT receive prophetx-update events (default)
  - true               → receive every ProphetX delta (all sports + kinds)
  - object with filters → receive only matching (sport, kind) deltas

The object form is optional in both dimensions:
  - `sports: ['basketball']` alone → all kinds for basketball
  - `kinds: ['prop']` alone        → all sports' props
  - both specified                 → intersection

Invalid filter values (unknown sport / kind) are silently dropped by the
server AFTER being received — the server never widens the subscription
to "all". See the server's validateSubscription() for exact semantics.

PropsEVOpportunity.description: One +EV price on a player prop (same math as {@link EVOpportunity}).

fairProbability.description: The conservative fair (the fair minus 1 point).

kind.description: `venue` for an exchange (Novig): never tradeable here, its depth is not checked on props.

PropsEVRow.description: A Pinnacle-priced player prop with its fair line and the prices that beat it.

opportunities.description: Best EV first; empty on a row listed only because `all: true`.

timestampUtc.description: `timestamp` in UTC, or `null` when its clock cannot be known; `timestamp` is the stored time (US Eastern for many rows stored before 2026-09-16). Added Oct 2026.
`timestamp` in UTC, or `null` when its clock cannot be known. Added Oct 2026.

books.description:
Per-requested-book feeder liveness. Added Sep 2026.

`ageSeconds` is how long since that book last PUBLISHED, not how old the price
is: pollers rewrite their cache on a cadence even when no line moved. There is
deliberately no aggregate status field — a book whose feeder dies drops off the
board rather than ageing, so a roll-up would report healthy for a dead book.

booksReturned.description: Books that actually contributed props to THIS response. Added Sep 2026.

fanduelMarketIds.description: getProps with `state`: the FanDuel marketId rewrite. Added Oct 2026.

marketIds.description: getBookProps("fanduel") with `state`: the marketId rewrite. Added Oct 2026.

retiredBooks.description:
Books named in `books` whose props are no longer on this board (bet365, polymarket),
each with where they are served now. Present only when one was named.

americanPrice.description: American price for a row whose side the book did not label (some alternate-line rows); null otherwise.

line.description: The line as stored, which may be a decimal string such as `"1.50"`.

lineValue.description: `line` as a number, always present; `null` when it is null or unparseable.

overPrice.description: `null` when the book offered no over side.

qualityFlags.description:
Known issues of this row (Oct 2026); an empty list when none applies. Some NHL rows carry
`prop_other_market_under_label`, `prop_two_markets_alternate`, `prop_two_markets_in_play` or
`prop_market_partly_wrong`: their prices are another market than `propType` and `line` say, or one of
two markets stored alternately under one key. Flagged rows are still returned; leave them out of
models and grading. `prop_two_markets_in_play` affects only rows recorded after the game started.

recordedAtUtc.description:
The capture time in UTC (ISO, ends in Z), or `null` when its clock cannot be known (rows stored
before 2026-03-28, and draftkings rows from 2026-03-28 04:00 to 2026-04-10). `recordedAt` is the
time as stored: fanduel and caesars rows before 2026-09-16, and draftkings before 2026-03-28 04:00,
hold US Eastern wall time even though the value ends in Z. Added Oct 2026: absent on an older API.

RawJson.description: The book's own JSON, served verbatim. Decode without strict typing.

RealtimeClientStreamPosition.description:
The stream position a `pinnacle-realtime` or `pinnacle-realtime-sync` frame
carries for its one sport.

checkpoint.description:
Set on the periodic checkpoint frame. `GET /{sport}/realtime` answers with a
`meta.stream` you align to these; see {@link RealtimeOddsPayload}.

epoch.description:
Opaque id of one run of the stream. A new epoch means the stream restarted and
its `seq` numbering started again: reload the board.

seq.description: Goes up by 1 per frame for the sport within one epoch.

RealtimeFeedState.description:
Why this response is empty, when it is.

`live`    — events were served.
`unknown` — we cannot tell whether the feed is idle or broken.

Deliberately only two states. Earlier drafts also had `idle` and `down`; both were
removed after measurement. `down` was unreachable. `idle` keyed on the upstream
reporting "connected, zero matchups", which it also reports when a live feed has
frozen — so it could have claimed "nothing on" during an outage. Judge with
`lastDataAgeSeconds`: a value in the hundreds of thousands means the feed has
produced nothing for days.

lastDataAgeSeconds.description:
Seconds since this sport last produced ANY data, or `null` if it has not been
observed producing data. `null` does NOT mean healthy, and does not mean zero.

resubscribing.description:
True while the feed is subscribing again after a reconnect, when some leagues
can be silent. `null` means unknown, by the same rules as `upstreamAgeSeconds`.
Absent from API versions that predate it.

stalled.description:
True when the board has an event in play (`phase: "live"`) and Pinnacle has sent
nothing for this sport for longer than its normal quiet spells during play: prices
can be out of date even though the board was rewritten seconds ago. False on a board
with nothing in play. `null` when `upstreamAgeSeconds` is null or the events carry no
