`phase`. It does not change `freshness.stale`. Absent from API versions that predate it.

upstreamAgeSeconds.description:
Seconds since Pinnacle last sent anything for this sport, as of this response.
`lastDataAgeSeconds` stays low while Pinnacle is quiet, because the board is
rewritten on a schedule either way; this keeps growing, so it is the field that
shows a feed that is running but hearing nothing.

`null` means unknown: always when `meta.source` is not `"pinnacle"`, and before
the feed has received anything since it started. Absent from API versions that
predate it.

RealtimeFrameFeed.description:
The sport's upstream feed state on every `pinnacle-realtime` and
`pinnacle-realtime-sync` frame: the same fields as REST `meta.feed`
({@link RealtimeFeedState}). `stalled: true` means prices can be out of date while
frames keep arriving. Each field is `null` when unknown.

RealtimeFreshness.description:
Freshness for the realtime endpoints, where `ageSeconds` can legitimately be
unknown.

Deliberately NOT a widening of {@link OddsFreshness}: `/odds` and `/events` share
that type and customers do arithmetic directly on their `ageSeconds`, so loosening
it there would force null-checks on consumers who do not need them today.

`ageSeconds: null` means the age is genuinely unmeasurable — no source produced
data and we have never observed this sport produce any. It replaced a reported
`0`, which claimed the freshest possible data on a feed that had served nothing
for four days. When null, `stale` is always `true`.

ageSeconds.description: Seconds since this data was produced, or `null` when that is unknowable.

droppedAsFinished.description: Events dropped because the match was confirmed finished (realtime only).

droppedAsStale.description:
Events dropped because their scheduled start is older than the sport's
max plausible live duration — a source-independent staleness guard
(realtime only).

feed.description: Added 2026-08-20. Optional so responses from older API builds still typecheck.

stream.description:
The `pinnacle-realtime` stream position this response matches, or `null` when
the response cannot be aligned with the stream (for example when it was served
from PS3838). Absent from API versions that predate it.

When it is set, `data` is the board at that position after your `league`
filter, so an empty `data` means no event matches, not a missing feed.
`pinnacle-realtime` frames are never filtered by league: if you load with
`league`, apply the same filter to every frame, or load without it. To follow
`pinnacle-realtime` without gaps, see the loading procedure on
{@link RealtimeOddsPayload}.

timestamp.description: Absent only on an empty response for a sport we have never seen produce data.

RealtimeOddsPayload.description:
Payload of the `pinnacle-realtime` and `ps3838-realtime` WebSocket events.

**Not the REST shape.** `GET /{sport}/realtime` returns `{ data: OddsEvent[], meta }`;
a frame is keyed by sport: `{ timestamp, <sport>: OddsEvent[], ... }`. Each frame
carries exactly one sport with at least one event. Read it with
{@link realtimeSportEvents }; `stream?.sport`, or the one key whose value is an array,
tells you which sport it is.

Both events go to connections on Hall of Fame, or on a plan with the WebSocket
add-on, for the sports in your subscription (every sport if you never subscribe).
`books` does not narrow them, and neither is filtered by league. A `ps3838-realtime`
frame can be several MB, so allow a client message size of at least 32 MB.

## `pinnacle-realtime`: every frame is partial (`delta: true`)

- Merge each event into your board by `id`, replacing the whole event, then delete
  the ids in `removed[<sport>]`.
- `resync: true` marks a frame from the periodic resend, which also carries events
  that have not changed.
- When present, `stream` is `{ sport, epoch, seq, checkpoint? }`. Within one epoch,
  `seq` goes up by 1 per frame for that sport. A frame whose seq is at or below the
  last one you applied is a duplicate: ignore it. A skipped seq, a new epoch, or a
  frame without `stream` after frames that had one means you must load the board
  again; keep your current board until the new one is ready.
- A stream position or removals for a sport with no events to send arrive on
  `pinnacle-realtime-sync` ({@link PinnacleRealtimeSyncPayload}). Handle both events.

**Loading a board.** On every connect and reconnect, and whenever the rules above
say so:
1. Buffer the sport's messages from both `pinnacle-realtime` and
   `pinnacle-realtime-sync`.
2. Wait up to 25 seconds for one with `stream.checkpoint` set. If the sport's
   frames carry no `stream`, go on at once.
3. Call `client.rest.getRealtime(sport)` and read `meta.stream`:
   - `null`: replace your board with `data`, merge every frame with no seq check,
     and load again after 10, 20, 40 seconds and so on, up to every 5 minutes.
   - its `epoch` differs from the checkpoint's, or its `seq` is lower than the
     checkpoint's: load again at the next checkpoint.
   - otherwise: replace your board with `data`, discard buffered messages with a
     seq at or below `meta.stream.seq`, and apply the rest in order.

Frames are not filtered by league. If you load with `league` (REST keeps events
whose `league` contains that text, ignoring case), apply the same filter to every
frame; otherwise load without it.

`removed` does not always list every event that leaves the board, and a sport
whose last event ends can stop sending. So also load a sport's board again when it
has sent no message for about 30 seconds, and every 5 minutes or so; each load
drops events that ended without being listed.

Each load counts against your request quota.

## `ps3838-realtime`: the frame says how to apply it

- `delta: true`: only the events that changed. Merge them by `id`.
- `snapshot: true`: the sport's full board. Replace your board for that sport. Sent
  about every 20 seconds, and sooner after an event leaves the board.
- Neither marker: also the sport's full board. Replace it.

A sport with no events sends nothing, so when a sport's last event ends no frame
says so. On every connect and reconnect, and whenever a sport has sent nothing for
about a minute, load its board from `client.rest.getPS3838Realtime(sport)` and
apply frames from there.

`ps3838-realtime` handlers share this type, so `stream`, `removed` and `resync` are
typed on them too; those fields are only sent on `pinnacle-realtime`.

delta.description:
The frame carries only changed events: merge them into your board by `id`. Set on
every `pinnacle-realtime` frame, and on `ps3838-realtime` delta frames.

feed.description: `pinnacle-realtime`: the sport's upstream feed state ({@link RealtimeFrameFeed}).

odds_format.description: Odds format hint from the upstream source. Prices on the realtime feeds are American odds (value: "american").

removed.description: `pinnacle-realtime`: event ids to delete from your board, keyed by sport.

resync.description: `pinnacle-realtime`: this frame comes from the periodic resend and can repeat unchanged events.

snapshot.description: `ps3838-realtime` only: the sport's full board. Replace your board for that sport.

stream.description: `pinnacle-realtime`: this sport's position on the stream, when the frame carries one.

RealtimeStreamPosition.description: A position on a realtime stream: `seq` counts frames for one sport within one `epoch`.

epoch.description:
Opaque id of one run of the stream. A new epoch means the stream restarted and
its `seq` numbering started again: reload the board.

seq.description: Goes up by 1 per frame for the sport within one epoch.

expire_previous_after_hours.description: How long the previous secret keeps signing beside the new one: 0 to 168 hours (default 24). 0 retires it at once.

ScoreClock.description:
The game clock of an in-play NBA, NHL, NFL or NCAAF game. Absent on every other
sport and whenever no clock was read for the game.

asOf.description: When the clock was read: tick secondsRemaining down from this instant while running.

period.description: The period the clock belongs to, in the source's numbering; status.period is the board's own.

running.description: True while the clock runs, false in a stoppage or intermission, null when the feed cannot say (NFL and NCAAF between plays; any game before its first movement).

secondsRemaining.description: Seconds left in the period; null when the source shows no clock (a shootout, for one).

baseballDetail.description: Baseball-specific live detail (inning, half, hits, errors, pitcher).

genericTeamStats.description:
Sport-specific aggregate team stats as a key-value map. For baseball this
carries the box score (hits, errors, homeRuns, runsBattedIn, leftOnBase,
walks, strikeouts, stolenBases, atBat, battingAverage, …).

incidents.description: Live match incidents — goals, cards, subs (soccer).

lastUpdated.description: Last time this event's CONTENT changed (score, status, linescores, …), not the poll time.

lineups.description: Starters + bench, when the source publishes them.

soccerDetail.description: Soccer result breakdown: normal time, extra time, penalty shootout.

sourceMatchId.description: Upstream match id, for correlating with the stats endpoints.

startTime.description: Null when the source did not supply a start time.

displayClock.description: Time left in the period for NBA/NHL/NFL/NCAAF games in play (5:32, or 48.3 under a minute); the soccer minute; null otherwise.

linescores.description:
Per-period scores. Quarters, sets, maps, or — for baseball — INNINGS.
A side that never batted in a half-inning (walk-off, or the home team
leading after the top of the 9th) simply has no entry for that period,
so the two sides' arrays can differ in length.

ScoreView.description:
One game on the `scores-update` WebSocket event: a lean view of a
{@link ScoreEvent} with the score, status and teams only. Linescores, stats,
lineups, incidents and sport-specific detail stay on `getScores()`.

lastUpdated.description:
In a `delta`, when this change happened. In a `full`, the game's own last
content change, as on `getScores()`.

startTime.description: Null when the source did not supply a start time.

ScoresUpdate.description:
Payload of the `scores-update` WebSocket event: live scores for ONE sport.

Opt in with `subscribe({ ..., scores: true })` (every sport) or
`scores: ['nfl', 'soccer']`; no `scores` field, no messages. Same access as the v2
events: Hall of Fame, or a paid plan with the WebSocket add-on.

- `full`: every game in play for `sport`, about every 30 seconds. Replace your live
  board for that sport. A sport with no game in play sends no `full`.
- `delta`: only what changed since the previous message: games in play whose score
  or state changed, games that just finished (`status.state === "post"` with the
  final score), and `removed`. Merge `events` by `id`, then drop the `removed` ids.

A score change goes out within about 1 second where the source pushes scores, and
within about 3 seconds otherwise. `getScores()` is unchanged.

removed.description:
`delta` only: ids of games that left the live board without a known final
state. Treat them as no longer live; `getScores()` has how they ended.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 time the message was built.

ServerHeartbeat.description:
`server-heartbeat`: sent every 10 seconds on every connection, independent of odds
traffic, so silence is detectable. `seq` is counted by the server, not per
connection: it goes up by 1 every 10 seconds and can jump ahead or start again from
1 after a reconnect. Compare it only within one connection, where a gap means
messages were missed.

ServerNotice.description:
`server-notice`: why the server closed your previous connection, sent once on the
next connect. `SERVER_RESTART` is the exception: it is sent to open connections
just before a restart, after which you reconnect (the SDK does) and send your
subscription again (the SDK does that too).

at.description: ISO time the connection was closed.

details.description: Measurements behind the decision, when there are any.

hint.description: What to change on your side.

socketId.description: Id of the connection that was closed, not the one receiving the notice.

ServerNoticeCode.description:
Why the server closed a connection, in {@link ServerNotice.code}. More codes can be
added.

- `BACKLOG_CAP`: more data was waiting to be sent to the connection than the
  per-connection limit allows.
- `AGGREGATE_SHED`: the connection was among those furthest behind while the
  server was shedding load.
- `GHOST`: data sent to the connection had not been read for over a minute.
- `SLOT_EVICTED`: closed to admit a new connection with the same API key, because it
  had stopped responding.
- `CLIENT_FRAME_LIMIT`: your client closed it because a message was larger than its
  maximum message size (close code 1009).
- `SERVER_RESTART`: sent to open connections just before a restart.

deadlineMs.description: The per-parlay deadline used, in ms.

quotesCached.description: Quotes answered from the cache (a repeated parlay counts once).

quotesMade.description: Quotes that reached a book's price request (each counted one build).

quotesPriced.description: Quotes that priced (a repeated parlay counts once).

SgpBatchMode.description:
`"book"`: every parlay on the one `book`. `"compare"`: every parlay on every
book (or `books`), as `compareSgp` prices one.

book.description: Mode `"book"` (required there): the one book every parlay is priced on.

books.description: Mode `"compare"`: the books to ask; default every book.

deadlineMs.description: How long each parlay waits for its books, 1000 to 15000 ms; default 6000.

fair.description: `true` adds our fair-price estimate to each parlay's result ({@link SgpFairBlock}).

parlays.description:
At most 10 parlays in mode `"book"`, 4 in mode `"compare"`. A parlay
repeated in one batch (same `eventId`, same legs in the same order) is
priced once and reported for each copy.

eventId.description: OUR event id for the game, as `getOdds` gives it (as on `compareSgp`).

ref.description: Your label for the parlay (up to 100 characters), returned with its result.

results.description: One per parlay, in request order.

SgpBatchResult.description:
One parlay's answer in a {@link SgpBatchResponse}, in request order. The
fields after `status` depend on the batch's `mode`:
- mode `"book"`: `book`, `bookStatus` and, as on a {@link SgpCompareBook},
  `bookEventId`, `httpStatus`, `result` (the `/sgp/build` body), `cached`, `reason`;
- mode `"compare"`: `best` and `books` (exactly what `compareSgp` returns).

With `fair: true`, `fair` is on every `done` result (`null` when nothing
priced). A `not-started` parlay carries no fair block: `fair` is `null` in mode
`"book"` and absent in mode `"compare"`.

best.description:
Mode `"compare"`: the highest decimal price among the books that priced,
or `null`.

bookEventId.description: Mode `"book"`: the book's own event id for the game, once it was mapped.

bookStatus.description:
Mode `"book"`: what happened on that book (the values a compare book's
`status` takes).

books.description: Mode `"compare"`: every book asked, each with its `status`.

cached.description: Mode `"book"`: `true` when `result` is a cached quote (no build counted).

fair.description: With `fair: true`: our estimate for this parlay, or `null` when nothing priced.

httpStatus.description: Mode `"book"`: the status `/sgp/build` would have answered with.

index.description: The parlay's index in your `parlays` array.

legsHash.description: A hash of the sport and legs (as `meta.legsHash` on `compareSgp`).

reason.description: Mode `"book"`: why the book was left out or not priced, when there is no `result`.

result.description: Mode `"book"`: exactly the `/sgp/build` body for this parlay, when the book answered.

status.description:
`"done"`: priced or answered. `"not-started"`: this parlay's pricing
would have begun more than about 20 seconds after the call began, so it was
not priced (except by any book answered from a cached quote); its builds are
given back while the minute they were counted in is still running. Send it
again.

SgpBookSelection.description:
The book's own ids for a resolved SGP leg on DraftKings, Hard Rock, BetRivers,
Bally Bet and BetMGM. Hard Rock's, BetRivers' and Bally Bet's are strings of
digits; BetMGM's `marketId` reads `v1:<fixture>:<market>` or
`v2:<fixture>:<market>`, and on NHL `sc:<fixture>:<builderId>` with the
option string BetMGM's bet builder lists as `selectionId`.

SgpBuildErrorBody.description:
The body of a thrown `buildSgp` failure that reached pricing, found on the
error as `err.details`; `err.code` is `reasonCode`:
- the no-price 503 (`ServiceBusyError`, `code` `no-price`): no usable answer
  came back; retry after `err.retryAfterMs`;
- the 502 older API versions sent for every refusal (`OwlsInsightError`,
  status 502). Current API versions return a refused parlay as a 422 on
  {@link SgpBuildResponse} instead, with the same fields.

Match on `reasonCode`, `legIndex`, `lineEchoed` and `failureCodes`, never on
`message`, which is prose.

failureCodes.description: Only when FanDuel rejected the parlay with its own failure codes.

legIndex.description: Only for the `line-*` codes: the leg's index in your `legs` array.

lineEchoed.description:
Only for the `line-*` codes: the line FanDuel priced, exactly as it sent
it, or `null` when it sent none.

SgpBuildMeta.description:
`meta` of a `buildSgp` response (200, the leg-resolution 422 and the refused
422), and of the no-price 503, `SGP_BUSY` 503 and legacy 502 error bodies.

The fields marked "API v2.348.0" are absent from older API versions.

book.description: The book the legs were resolved and priced against (`"fanduel"`, `"draftkings"`, ...).

catalogAgeMs.description:
The MINIMUM age, in ms, the catalog data already had at `resolvedAt`; the
true age can be higher. Omitted when the age is unknown. API v2.348.0.

eventId.description:
The event id as the API echoes it: a number on FanDuel, a string on every
other book (digits, or BetMGM NFL's `"6:43680"`).

lineUnverified.description:
`true` on a 200 that priced at least one leg whose line the book's
response does not confirm (FanDuel's alternate N-or-more strikeout rungs;
every BetMGM NHL leg, whose price answer names no leg). Absent when every
line was confirmed. API v2.348.0.

lineUnverifiedLegs.description:
With `lineUnverified`: the indexes of those legs in your `legs` array.
API v2.348.0.

priceRequestedAt.description:
When the price request went out, on the API server's clock. Present on
every 200, and on a refused 422, a no-price 503 or a legacy 502 only when
FanDuel returned a response. Absent on a leg-resolution 422 (nothing was
priced). API v2.348.0.

pricedAt.description:
When FanDuel's answer came back, on the API server's clock. Never earlier
than `priceRequestedAt`; this is the quote time to use. Same presence as
`priceRequestedAt`. API v2.348.0.

resolvedAt.description:
When the legs were resolved against FanDuel's catalog, before pricing.
API v2.348.0.

timestamp.description:
The same instant as `resolvedAt`: when the legs were resolved, BEFORE
pricing. It is not the quote time; use `pricedAt` for that.

book.description:
Sportsbook to price the parlay against: `"fanduel"`, `"draftkings"`,
`"hardrock"`, `"betrivers"`, `"ballybet"` or `"betmgm"`. Any other value is
a 400 with code `SGP_BOOK_UNSUPPORTED` listing `supportedBooks`.

eventId.description: Pass as a string. Use `String(event.eventId)` when sourced from `getSgpEvents`.

fair.description:
`true` adds our fair-price estimate as `fair` on a priced 200
({@link SgpFairBlock}). MVP and Hall of Fame plans: on a lower plan the
build is a 403 `SGP_TIER_REQUIRED` (`ForbiddenError`), refused before
anything is priced and not counted against any limit; a 503
`SGP_FEATURE_DISABLED` means the fair price is not switched on yet.
API v2.515.0.

SgpBuildResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/v1/{sport}/sgp/build`.

Also what a 422 returns. A 422 is NOT thrown, so check `success` before
reading `sgp`, then branch on `reasonCode` (the API sends it on every 422 since
the refusal-status change; older API versions sent none on a leg-resolution 422
and threw the refusal as a 502):
- `"unresolved"`: a leg could not be resolved. No `sgp`, and a `reason` on each
 unresolved leg naming which lines FanDuel does offer or why the category,
 side or leg type cannot work. Fix the legs.
- any other {@link SgpReasonCode} (`line-mismatch`, `bet-failure`,
 `not-placeable`, ...): FanDuel judged the slip and refused it, or its answer
 did not confirm the legs as sent. The request was valid but cannot be priced
 as specified, so do not resend the same body unchanged. `legIndex`,
 `lineEchoed` and `failureCodes` are set where they apply; `message` is prose.

Every other failure throws: a `ServiceBusyError` with `code` `no-price` when no
usable answer came back (503, retry after `retryAfterMs`), one with an `SGP_*`
code ({@link SgpErrorBody} in `details`), or, from older API versions, an
`OwlsInsightError` with status 502 whose `details` is the
{@link SgpBuildErrorBody}.

failureCodes.description:
Refused parlay only, when FanDuel rejected it with its own failure codes
(e.g. `SELECTION_NOT_FOUND`).

fair.description:
Present on a priced 200 when the request sent `fair: true` (MVP / Hall of
Fame): our estimate of the parlay's price, beside the book's `sgp`, never in
place of it. API v2.515.0.

legIndex.description: Refused parlay, `line-*` codes only: the leg's index in your `legs` array.

lineEchoed.description:
Refused parlay, `line-*` codes only: the line FanDuel priced, exactly as it
sent it, or `null` when it sent none.

message.description:
Refused parlay (422) only: human-readable prose. Match on `reasonCode`,
`legIndex`, `lineEchoed` and `failureCodes`, never on this.

pricing.description:
`"<book>-slip"` on a 200 (`"fanduel-slip"`, `"draftkings-slip"`, ...): the
price is that book's own bet-slip answer.

reasonCode.description:
Present when `success: false`: `"unresolved"` on a leg-resolution 422,
otherwise the {@link SgpReasonCode} of a refused parlay (never `no-price`,
which is thrown as a 503). Absent from older API versions' leg-resolution
422.

SgpCompareBook.description: One book's answer in a {@link SgpCompareResponse}.

bookEventId.description: The book's own event id for the game, once it was mapped.

cached.description: `true` when `result` is a cached quote (no build was counted for it).

httpStatus.description:
The status `/sgp/build` would have answered with, when the book was priced
or refused.

ms.description: How long this book took, in ms (mapping and pricing).

reason.description: Why the book was left out or not priced, when there is no `result` to say it.

result.description: Exactly the `/sgp/build` body for this book, when it answered.

SgpCompareBookResult.description:
A book's `result` in a comparison: exactly the body `/sgp/build` returned for
that book. Which fields are set depends on the book's `status`: a priced 200
(`sgp`, `legs`, `meta`), a refused or unresolved 422 (`reasonCode`, `legs`,
...), a no-price or busy 503 (`code`, `legs`, `meta`), or a short
`{ error, message }` (an unknown game, or too few legs resolved). Every field is
therefore optional here: branch on the book's `status` first.

SgpCompareBookStatus.description:
What happened on one book in a comparison:
- `priced`: `result` is the book's 200 body (`sgp` is its price).
- `refused`: the book refused the parlay; `result` is its 422 body (`reasonCode`).
- `unresolved`: a leg did not resolve on that book (for example a different
  main line); `result` says which and why.
- `busy`, `no-price`: that book produced no usable answer; retry later.
- `timeout`: the book had not answered when `deadlineMs` ran out, or was not
  reached in time.
- `event-not-listed`: the book does not list this game for same game parlays.
- `ambiguous-event`: two games match (a doubleheader without `-G2`), or the
  book lists this matchup at a different start, so it is a different game.
- `unsupported`: the book does not price this sport or one of the legs (`reason`).
- `disabled`: that book's pricing is paused.
- `skipped`: `fanduel: "skip"`.

New statuses can appear: handle the ones you know and treat the rest as "no price".

booksCached.description: Books answered from a cached quote.

booksQuoted.description: Books that reached a book's price request (each counted one build).

legsHash.description: A hash of the sport and legs: the same parlay always hashes the same.

books.description:
The books to ask (`"fanduel"`, `"draftkings"`, `"hardrock"`,
`"betrivers"`, `"ballybet"`, `"betmgm"`); default every book.

deadlineMs.description:
How long to wait for the books, 1000 to 15000 ms; default 6000. Keep the
client's `timeout` above it.

eventId.description:
OUR event id for the game, as `getOdds` gives it:
`{sport}:{Away}@{Home}-{YYYYMMDD}`, with `-G2` for the second game of a
doubleheader. Not a book's id from `getSgpEvents`.

fair.description:
`true` adds our fair-price estimate as `fair`, built from every book that
priced ({@link SgpFairBlock}).

fanduel.description:
`"cold"` (the default): FanDuel prices in a fresh browser session and is
given at least 12000 ms. `"skip"`: FanDuel is left out (`status: "skipped"`).

fresh.description: `true` never uses a cached quote: every book is priced now.

legs.description: The same legs `buildSgp` takes, 1 to 12, sent to every book.

best.description: The highest decimal price among the books that priced, or `null` when none did.

books.description: Every book asked, priced or not, each with its `status`.

fair.description:
With `fair: true`: our estimate from every book that priced, or `null` when
no book priced. Absent without `fair: true`.

SgpCompareResultMeta.description:
`meta` of a book's `result` in a comparison: the build's meta, plus the cache
label when the answer was a cached quote.

book.description: The book the legs were resolved and priced against (`"fanduel"`, `"draftkings"`, ...).

cacheAgeMs.description: With `cached`: the quote's age in ms.

cached.description:
`true` when this answer is a quote the book priced for exactly these legs
and this game in the last 15 seconds (`pricedAt` still says when).

catalogAgeMs.description:
The MINIMUM age, in ms, the catalog data already had at `resolvedAt`; the
true age can be higher. Omitted when the age is unknown. API v2.348.0.

eventId.description:
The event id as the API echoes it: a number on FanDuel, a string on every
other book (digits, or BetMGM NFL's `"6:43680"`).

lineUnverified.description:
`true` on a 200 that priced at least one leg whose line the book's
response does not confirm (FanDuel's alternate N-or-more strikeout rungs;
every BetMGM NHL leg, whose price answer names no leg). Absent when every
line was confirmed. API v2.348.0.

lineUnverifiedLegs.description:
With `lineUnverified`: the indexes of those legs in your `legs` array.
API v2.348.0.

priceRequestedAt.description:
When the price request went out, on the API server's clock. Present on
every 200, and on a refused 422, a no-price 503 or a legacy 502 only when
FanDuel returned a response. Absent on a leg-resolution 422 (nothing was
priced). API v2.348.0.

pricedAt.description:
When FanDuel's answer came back, on the API server's clock. Never earlier
than `priceRequestedAt`; this is the quote time to use. Same presence as
`priceRequestedAt`. API v2.348.0.

resolvedAt.description:
When the legs were resolved against FanDuel's catalog, before pricing.
API v2.348.0.

timestamp.description:
The same instant as `resolvedAt`: when the legs were resolved, BEFORE
pricing. It is not the quote time; use `pricedAt` for that.

competition.description: FanDuel's competition name; empty when unknown.

eventId.description:
The book's event id: a number on the wire on FanDuel, a string on every
other book (digits, or BetMGM NFL's `"6:43680"`). Pass it to `buildSgp` as
`String(event.eventId)`.

start.description: Scheduled start (ISO 8601), or `null` when FanDuel lists none.

book.description: The book the events belong to (`"fanduel"`).

SgpFairBlock.description:
Our estimate of a same game parlay's price (`fair` on {@link SgpBuildResponse}
and {@link SgpCompareResponse}), built from de-vigged leg probabilities. It is
never a sportsbook's price: the book's own quote stays in `sgp`.

The legs' probabilities are multiplied and adjusted by how the book itself
priced these legs together: `basis.correlationFactor` is the product of the
book's single prices divided by its parlay price (on compare, the median across
the books that priced). That factor also keeps the book's parlay surcharge over
its singles (`basis.marginAdjusted` is `false`), so the estimate removes the
singles' vig, not that surcharge.

`price` is `null`, with `why`, when any leg has no fair (`coverage.missingLegs`
and each leg's `why` say which), when no book returned a usable single price
for every leg or the factor fell outside 0.25 to 4, once the game has started,
or when the fair could not be worked out in time.

correlation.description: `"book-implied"`: read off the books' own quotes.

correlationFactor.description: The correlation factor used, or `null` when none was usable.

correlationSources.description: Each priced book's own factor (`null` when that book's quote gave none).

legs.description: `"fair-v1"`: each leg's `source` says whether Pinnacle anchored it.

marginAdjusted.description: `false`: the factor keeps the book's parlay surcharge over its singles.

booksDisagree.description: Some leg's fair is one other books' prices disagree with (each leg says which).

computedAt.description: ISO 8601: when the estimate was worked out.

missingLegs.description: Indexes (in your `legs` array) of the legs with no fair.

estimate.description: Always `true`: this is an estimate, not a book's price.

independent.description: The same legs treated as unrelated (no correlation), or `null`.

label.description: `"Owls Insight estimate, not a sportsbook price"`.

price.description: The fair price of the parlay with the books' correlation, or `null` with `why`.

why.description:
Why `price` is `null`, or `null` when there is a price. Known values:
`missing-leg-fair`, `no-correlation`, `not-a-probability`, `in-play`. New
values can appear.

SgpFairLeg.description:
One leg's fair probability in an {@link SgpFairBlock}: our Fair v1 fair for the
leg, the one `/api/v1/{sport}/fair` serves for a moneyline, spread or total (a
spread or total only at that fair's own number, never a whole number) and the
one `/api/v1/{sport}/props/ev` scores a player prop against (x.5 lines).

ageMs.description: Age in ms of the fair board the leg was read from, or `null`.

booksDisagree.description: Other books' prices disagree with this leg's fair.

legIndex.description: The leg's index in your `legs` array.

line.description:
The number the fair is at (the spread or total point, the prop line);
`null` for a moneyline and without a fair.

pinnacleLine.description:
With `why: "line-not-at-pinnacle-number"`: the number Pinnacle has, for
the leg's side.

probability.description: The leg's fair (no-vig) probability, or `null` with `why` when it has none.

source.description:
How the fair was made: `"pinnacle"` (Pinnacle-anchored) or, for a
moneyline, `"consensus"` (three or more books agreed). `null` without a fair.

why.description:
Why the leg has no fair, or `null` when it has one. Known values:
`fair-board-unavailable` (no board, or one too old to use),
`game-not-on-fair-board`, `ambiguous-game`, `team-not-matched`,
`side-not-matched`, `no-line`, `whole-number-line`,
`line-not-at-pinnacle-number` (see `pinnacleLine`),
`category-not-on-fair-board`, `prop-not-on-fair-board`, `ambiguous-player`,
`no-fair`, `in-play`, `fair-unavailable` (not worked out in time). New
values can appear.

SgpFairPrice.description:
A probability with its prices: decimal odds, and American odds rounded to a
whole number.

SgpFdSelection.description:
The FanDuel selection a resolved SGP leg maps to. `marketId` is specific to
the FanDuel state that priced it (New Jersey); `selectionId` is the same in
every state.

period.description: NHL, Hard Rock: the period's result instead of the full game.

selection.description: The team. With a `period`, the period's 3-way result: a team or `"Tie"`.

period.description: NHL, Hard Rock: the period's spread at a line Hard Rock lists for it.

point.description:
The book's main line, or on NHL an alternate puck line Hard Rock,
Bally Bet or (before the game) DraftKings lists.

period.description: NHL, Hard Rock: the period's total at a line Hard Rock lists for it.

point.description:
The book's main line, or on NHL an alternate total Hard Rock, Bally
Bet or (before the game) DraftKings lists.
A line Hard Rock lists for that team.

team.description: The team whose total it is.

type.description: One team's own full-game total (Hard Rock NHL).

category.description:
Player-prop categories differ per sport (full lists at
https://owlsinsight.com/docs#sub-sgp):
- MLB: `strikeouts` [ks], `hits`, `total-bases` [tb], `home-runs` [hr],
  `rbis` [rbi], `runs`, `stolen-bases` [sb, steals], `singles`,
  `doubles`, `triples`, `hits-runs-rbis`.
- WNBA: `points`, `rebounds` verified; `assists`, `threes`, `steals`,
  `blocks` accepted but not verified, so a leg may be refused.
- NBA: `points`, `rebounds`, `assists`, `threes`, `steals`, `blocks`,
  all accepted but not verified.
- NFL, NCAAF, NHL, NCAAB, soccer, tennis: no player props. The leg is
  refused (422) naming the category you sent and, for a betting-name
  alias, the props category it stands for, e.g.
  `'anytime_touchdown' (touchdowns)`.

line.description:
The half-point below the threshold: `0.5` = 1 or more, `1.5` = 2 or
more. `total-bases` has no 1+ market, so its lowest line is `1.5`.

player.description:
Full player name. A partial name is accepted but 422s if it matches
more than one player on the slate (e.g. "Ramirez").

side.description:
On MLB, only `strikeouts` accepts `"under"`: the batter categories are
FanDuel "N or more" markets and so are over-only. NBA/WNBA legs take
either side of the full-game line.

SgpLeg.description: A single leg in a Same Game Parlay build request.

SgpPeriod.description:
One period of an NHL game: the 1st, 2nd or 3rd period. A moneyline, spread or
total leg with a `period` prices that period instead of the full game; only
Hard Rock prices period legs, and every other book refuses them (422).

SgpPrice.description: The computed parlay price from a successful `buildSgp` call.

isSGM.description:
Always `true` on a 200: the price is the book's correlated same-game price
for exactly the legs sent.

SgpResolvedLeg.description: A single leg echoed back in a `buildSgp` response, with its resolution.

bookSelection.description:
Present when `resolved: true` on every book but FanDuel: that book's own ids
for the leg (only one of `fdSelection` and `bookSelection` is present).

description.description: Present when `resolved: true`: the FanDuel selection it resolved to.

fdSelection.description: Present when `resolved: true` on FanDuel: the FanDuel selection the leg resolved to.

reason.description: Present when `resolved: false`: why the leg could not be used.

single.description: On a 200: the leg's stand-alone price, or `null` when none was matched.

SoccerPlayDetail.description:
Soccer: a play is a match incident (type `Goal`, `Own goal`, `Penalty`, `Yellow Card`,
`Red Card`, `Substitution`), with the match minute, the player and, per type, the assist
(goal), the player going off (substitution: the play's `player` is the one coming on) or
the card. `clock` on the play is the minute as shown ("45+2"); `secondsRemaining` and
`wallclock` are null; `period` is the half (1, 2; 3 and 4 extra time; 5 penalties).

addedMinutes.description: Stoppage-time minutes (2 for "45+2"); null when none.

code.description: The source's own numeric incident code.

note.description: The source's note on the incident when it carries one.

SoccerPlayer.description: One player on a soccer play; `id` is null when the source names the player without an id.

SoccerScoreDetail.description:
Soccer result breakdown. `home.score`/`away.score` (and `score` on the stats
endpoints) are the score of the match itself, after extra time when it was
played, and NEVER include shootout goals; the shootout is only in `penalties`.

decidedBy.description: How a finished match was decided. Absent while in play.

extraTime.description: Score at the end of extra time. Only when extra time was played.

penalties.description: Penalty shootout score. Only when a shootout was played.

regulation.description: Score at the end of normal time.

SplitsBookEntry.description:
One book's figures for a game. A market the book has not published for the game is
absent, not zero, and so is any percentage a book does not publish: BetMGM publishes
ticket percentages only, so a `betmgm` entry carries the `*_bets_pct` fields and no
`*_handle_pct` fields. Treat every field below `book`/`title` as possibly absent.

as_of.description:
ISO 8601 time this book's figures were read. The books are read on different
schedules, so two books on one game can show different times. DraftKings figures
run until kickoff; the last pre-game DraftKings figures stay on the board for up to
4 hours after kickoff, with the `as_of` of that last read.
Absent on responses from before 2026-09-27.

book.description:
Book key: 'dk' (DraftKings), 'betmgm' (BetMGM, tickets only, since 2026-09-29) or
'circa' (Circa Sports). Other keys may appear as books are added.

away_team.description: The /odds team name (same string as {@link OddsEvent.away_team}).

event_id.description:
Our event id: the {@link OddsEvent.eventId} that `/api/v1/{sport}/odds` gives the
same game, `{sport}:{Away}@{Home}-{YYYYMMDD}` (e.g.
"nfl:Carolina Panthers@Cleveland Browns-20260927"), so splits join to odds on it.
The date is the game's UTC start date, except MLB games starting from
2026-10-11T10:00Z, which carry the US Eastern date (as on /odds). A game not on
/odds gets an id built the same way from its scheduled start. Both games of a
doubleheader share one `event_id`, as on /odds.

Before 2026-09-27 this was an upstream game code (e.g. "20260622MLB00030") that did
not match /odds.

home_team.description: The /odds team name (same string as {@link OddsEvent.home_team}).

SplitsHistoryRow.description:
One recorded reading of one book's splits for one game. Same shape as a
{@link SplitsBookEntry} on the live board, plus the game's `event_id` and `sport`, with
`recorded_at` where the live board has `as_of`. A row is written when the book's
figures (percentages, line or price) change, and again after 24 hours without a
change, so consecutive rows can carry the same figures.

A market absent from a row was not quoted at that read, and a percentage absent from
a market is not zero (BetMGM rows carry ticket percentages only).

event_id.description: The game's /odds eventId, the same as {@link SplitsGame.event_id}.

recorded_at.description: ISO 8601 time this reading was recorded.

age_seconds.description: Only when `status` is 'stale': how old the served board is, in seconds.

as_of.description:
ISO time of the OLDEST of the books' latest reads behind this board, so it never
overstates freshness. Each split also carries its own {@link SplitsBookEntry.as_of};
a DraftKings split kept after kickoff has an older one than this.
Since API v2.362.0.

books.description:
The books on this board: 'draftkings', 'betmgm' and, while it is offered, 'circa'.
Can be `['draftkings']` alone. (Each split's own `book` key is 'dk', 'betmgm' or
'circa'.) Read the book set from here, never from a fixed list: books are added.

source.description:
A fixed legacy value, 'circa_dk', whatever books are on the board. Do not read
the book set from it: use `books`.

status.description:
'ok' = every book on offer has a recent read. 'partial' = one does not (see
`partial_reason`), so `data` may be a subset. 'stale' = no book has a recent read,
and the last full board (at most 12 hours old, see `as_of` / `age_seconds`) is
served instead.
Absent on API versions before v2.346.0; 'stale' since v2.362.0.

total_games.description: Number of games in `data`. Present on every response since API v2.346.0 (earlier: only on cache misses).

StakeBet.description: One public sportsbook bet from Stake. Bettor identity is never returned.

amount.description: Stake on the whole slip, in `currency`. null when the bettor hid it.

createdAt.description: RFC-1123, passed through from upstream (e.g. 'Tue, 01 Sep 2026 16:10:32 GMT').

currency.description: The bettor's own currency, fiat or crypto (usdt, inr, sol, ngn, ...). NOT converted.

outcomes.description: More than one leg means a parlay, so `amount` cannot be attributed to one market.

StakeBetLeg.description: One leg of a public Stake bet. `amount` is on the SLIP, not the leg.

odds.description: Decimal odds AT PLACEMENT for this leg.

outcome.description:
outcome.id and market.id share a namespace with `getStakeV2()`, so a leg joins
directly to a board outcome. `fixture.id` does NOT join: the board uses a different
identifier for the same fixture. Join on outcome or market id, never fixture id.

StakeBetLegFixture.description:
The fixture of a Stake bet leg. `id` is a UUID in a DIFFERENT id space from the
board and joins to nothing there: join a wager to `getStakeV2()` by `slug`, whose
numeric prefix is the board fixture id ("46853667-sporting-galatasaray-istanbul"
is board fixture 46853667).

tournament.description:
The competition, so a wager can be attributed without matching it to a board
first. `category` is a grouping (UEFA Champions League gives "International
Clubs"), NOT a sport: there is no sport field and no tournament-to-sport lookup.

ageSeconds.description: Seconds since `timestamp`. null whenever `timestamp` is null; never derive freshness from a null timestamp.

now.description: Response clock, ISO, present on every shape.

oldestBetTime.description: ISO-8601, unlike the RFC-1123 `createdAt` inside `data[]`. null on empty shapes.

timestamp.description: ISO time of the worker write this response serves. null on no-data and partial-miss: there is no data to date.

StakeBetsSampling.description:
Capture-rate facts. `complete` is always false: upstream caps each query at 50 rows
with no cursor and the feed turns over faster than that, so the window is a SAMPLE.
Total handle is NOT derivable from it.

observedNewPerMinute.description: Measured: null on empty shapes, and on a healthy response until a rate has been measured (normal right after a restart).

pollIntervalMs.description: Worker poll interval. Reported on empty shapes too while the feed has run in the last day; null only when even that is unknown.

windowSeconds.description: Measured: null on no-data and partial-miss.

StatsGame.description: One match from GET /api/v1/{sport}/stats: live, scheduled or finished today.

lastUpdated.description: Last time the score or state changed.

score.description: Null for a scheduled match (never a 0-0). Soccer: excludes shootout goals.

teamStats.description: A pair is null (or absent) when the source did not measure it, never a fake 0.

scheduledAndFinishedAsOf.description: When the scheduled and finished data was refreshed.

timestamp.description: When the live data was refreshed.

books.description:
Books for `odds-update` and `esports-update`. An empty or missing list, or one in
which no entry is a valid book, means every book. It does not narrow the realtime
events.

esportsRealtime.description:
Per-game Pinnacle esports realtime subscription. Opt-in; each game
requires a `league` substring filter. The server emits one event per
game: `cs2-realtime`, `lol-realtime`, `valorant-realtime`, `dota2-realtime`.

exclude_exchanges.description:
`true` removes the exchange books (`kalshi`, `polymarket`, `novig`) from `books`,
so `odds-update` (and `esports-update`) leave them out; if only exchange books were
listed, every other book is used. Echoed in the `subscribed` acknowledgement.

oneXBetSoccer.description:
Opt-in to the isolated 1xBet SOCCER feed (`1xbet-update` events). Default:
not subscribed. 1xBet soccer is NOT in /odds — it's a scrape-based feed on
its own channel. (1xBet esports is unaffected and stays in the odds stream.)

plays.description:
Opt-in to play-by-play on the `plays-update` event ({@link PlaysUpdate}): `true`
for nba, nhl, nfl and ncaaf, or an array of those keys. Default: not subscribed.
Same access as `scores`. `getPlays()` works either way.

prophetx.description:
Opt-in to ProphetX exchange deltas. Default: not subscribed.
Pass `true` for the firehose, or an object to filter by sport/kind.
See `ProphetXSubscription` for shape details.

realtime.description:
Realtime feed opt-out. Default: every subscribed sport gets both
`pinnacle-realtime` and `ps3838-realtime`. `{ ps3838: false }` stops
`ps3838-realtime` for this connection and keeps `pinnacle-realtime`. Only a literal
`false` is honoured. `updateSubscription()` replaces the whole object.

scores.description:
Opt-in to live scores on the `scores-update` event ({@link ScoresUpdate}).
`true` for every sport, or an array of sport keys. Default: not subscribed.
Unknown keys are dropped, and an array with no valid key subscribes to nothing.
Same access as the v2 events. `getScores()` works either way.

sports.description:
Sports for `odds-update` and for the realtime events (`pinnacle-realtime`,
`pinnacle-realtime-sync`, `ps3838-realtime`). An empty list, or one in which no
entry is a valid sport, means every sport. The `subscribed` acknowledgement lists
the sports in force.

v2.description:
Opt-in to Source API (v2) raw pass-through WebSocket events
(`draftkings-v2-update`, `fanduel-v2-update`, `versus-v2-update`,
`bet365-v2-update`, `mybookie-v2-update`, `thunderpick-v2-update`,
`kalshi-v2-update`, `polymarket-v2-update`, and `betonline-realtime`
— BetOnline is the ONLY book whose event breaks the `-v2-update`
convention; assume the convention holds for every other book).
Default: not subscribed. See {@link V2Subscription} for the shape.

TennisScoreDetail.description: Tennis-specific live detail (games within sets, current game points, serving).

currentGameScore.description: Current game points (e.g. "40" vs "A"). Absent between games.

sets.description: Games won by each player in each set, e.g. [{home:6,away:4},{home:3,away:2}].

ThunderpickV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Thunderpick v2 events.

Each Thunderpick sport is a single stream (no per-league
segmentation). Pass `'*'` per sport you want. Arrays are accepted
and coerced to `'*'` server-side.

description.description: Up to 200 characters; an empty string clears it.

enabled.description:
false stops deliveries and cancels the undelivered ones. true resumes an endpoint
that you disabled or that was disabled after failing, and resets its failure count.

filters.description: Merged into the stored filters (see WebhookFiltersInput).

V2BookResponse.description: Any v2 book's raw board. `data` is keyed by the book's market or event id and holds the book's own JSON. `league` is null on a merged response, which then lists `leagues`.

V2LeagueFilter.description:
Per-sport league filter for v2 WebSocket subscriptions. Use `'*'` to
receive every league for that sport, or an array of league keys to
filter to a specific set. League keys come from the corresponding
`/leagues` REST endpoint.

accepted.description: What the connection is subscribed to for this book and sport: the keys, `['*']`, or `[]`.

leaguesEndpoint.description: Where to list the league keys that carry data, when the book has an index.

outcome.description:
- `unverified`: the league keys were accepted as written; a key that no book
  uses simply never receives anything.
- `no-valid-keys`: no usable key, so this sport was not subscribed for the book.
- `coerced-to-wildcard`: this book and sport carry no league key, so the
  filter was replaced with `'*'`.

rejectedCount.description: How many entries were dropped as invalid league keys.

rejectedSample.description: Up to 5 of the dropped values, truncated.

V2LeagueSlice.description: One league's share of a merged response: the `data` keys it contributed.

defaultExcluded.description: On a default request: the entries the book leaves out by default (DraftKings `props-*`, Fanatics Markets `books-*`, Polymarket US `full-*`), with the `marketIds` value that includes them.

marketAges.description: Seconds since each returned entry was last confirmed, by entry id, when the book sends it.

marketIds.description: Echo of the `marketIds` filter you sent (normalized), when you sent one.

marketsFilteredOut.description: With a `marketIds` filter: how many stored entries it left out.

accepted.description: What the subscription holds for `field` after validation.

outcome.description:
- `unverified`: `marketTypes` were accepted as written; a value no market
  carries never matches.
- `invalid-values-dropped`: some `eventTypes` were not event types.
- `no-valid-values-default-applied`: nothing usable, so the default applies.
- `coerced-to-wildcard-room-cap`: the filter was widened to `'*'` to stay under
  the per-connection limit. You receive more than you asked for, never less.
- `ignored-no-sports`: options without a valid sport subscribe to nothing.
- `not-yet-available`: an event type this connection does not receive yet
  (`accepted: []`, the type in `rejectedSample`), or that is accepted and
  starts arriving once it is enabled (`accepted: [type]`).

More outcomes can be added.

rejectedSample.description: Up to 5 of the dropped values, truncated.

sport.description: Set when the entry is about one sport (a league list widened to `'*'`).

V2Subscription.description:
Opt-in subscription for raw pass-through Source API (v2) WebSocket
events. Pass on `subscribe()` to start receiving the corresponding
`<book>-v2-update` events. Omit (or set the book to `undefined`) to
receive nothing for that book — these events are opt-in only.

4casters.description:
Delivers `4casters-v2-update`. A peer-to-peer EXCHANGE: each entry is a whole
event carrying its order book, every offer with its own price and the size
left on it. Odds are AMERICAN and may carry a half point. Quoted key because
the book's name starts with a digit.

⚠️ KEEP YOUR BASE `sports`/`books` SUBSCRIPTION NARROW when you use this.
On connect the server queues the whole initial odds snapshot (~6 MB, ~3,178
games) into your socket BEFORE any v2 delivery, and a socket whose backlog
passes 8 MB is force-disconnected. Subscribing to every sport and book and
then adding a large v2 filter can cross that cap on the first sweep, so you
reconnect in a loop and receive nothing — with no error naming the cause.
Measured: `{nfl, soccer, esports, mlb}` on top of the default subscription
reconnected 18 times and received zero events; the same client with
`sports:['nfl'], books:['pinnacle']` held one connection and received
events immediately.

⚠️ PREFER PER-LEAGUE FILTERS OVER `'*'` FOR SOCCER — it is 37 leagues and
~6 MB, republished whole on a sweep. `nfl` is ~1 MB, `esports` under 1 MB.

A league only pushes while it holds a live or imminent game (30s tier);
everything else moves on a 150s sweep and only when something changed. So
subscribing to `nfl` midweek and seeing nothing is correct, not broken.

ballybet.description:
Delivers `ballybet-v2-update`. Same Kambi platform, sports and payload
shape as betrivers, with Bally Bet's own prices.

bet105.description: Delivers `bet105-v2-update`. Same Ganchrow platform as betus; a Pinnacle mirror at -105.

betrivers.description: Delivers `betrivers-v2-update`. Kambi platform; deep player props.

betus.description: Delivers `betus-v2-update`. Each `markets[].data` is a whole EVENT.

lowvig.description: Delivers `lowvig-v2-update`. Same upstream as betonline, different prices.

propbuilder.description:
Prop Builder. Delivers `propbuilder-v2-update`. Every sport is one
league: pass `'*'` (`{ nfl: '*' }`). Pregame player props and game markets,
odds DECIMAL; changed entries are pushed within seconds, each one whole.

tippmixpro.description:
TippmixPro (Hungary, EveryMatrix). Multi-league sports need league keys
(from getTippmixproV2Leagues); nfl/ncaaf/nba/ncaab/nhl/mlb take `'*'`.
Deltas are PUSHED as upstream changes them, one market per entry.

V2Update.description: Payload of a `{book}-v2-update` WebSocket event. Two shapes exist: most books send a batch (`markets` is an array of `{ marketId, hash, kind, data }`), while fanduel, draftkings and versus send one market per event (`marketId`, `hash`, `data`, with `markets` a count). `timestamp` is epoch milliseconds on most books and an ISO string on some. Fields that differ between books are left untyped; decode `markets`, `timestamp`, `data` and `raw` accordingly.

heartbeat.description: Pinnacle: a heartbeat frame; with `matchupIds` it restates the league's full set.

matchupIds.description: Pinnacle: the league's current matchup ids. Drop any you hold that are not listed.

removedGhids.description: MyBookie: games that left the league: delete them.

removedIds.description: Ids of entries that left the league: delete them.

removedMatchupIds.description: Pinnacle: matchups that left the league: delete them.

VersusV2BookSubscription.description:
Per-book subscription shape for Versus (versus.es) v2 events.

Every versus sport is multi-league — filter by specific league keys
(from {@link OwlsInsightRest.getVersusV2Leagues }) or `'*'` for all leagues.
Only the sports listed here push `versus-v2-update` deltas; the remaining
REST-only versus sports are omitted because they never broadcast.

data.description: The endpoint and its signing secret, which is returned here and by rotate-secret only.

has_more.description: True when older deliveries remain: ask for the next page starting after the last `id`.

WebhookDelivery.description: One delivery to an endpoint, as the deliveries listing returns it.

last_status_code.description: Your receiver's last HTTP status, or null.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due, while `pending`; otherwise null.

payload.description: The exact body sent, or null.

response_excerpt.description: Up to the first 512 bytes of your receiver's last answer.

WebhookDeliveryPayload.description: A delivery body as stored, with `data` untyped: its shape depends on `type`.

endpoint_id.description: The endpoint it was sent to, `whk_...`.

expires_at.description: No delivery is attempted after this (ISO 8601).

id.description: The event id, `evt_...`: identical on every retry and in the `Owls-Webhook-Id` header. Dedupe on it.

occurred_at.description: When what it reports happened, as far as is known (ISO 8601).

type.description: The event type; a type added later arrives as a string this version does not list.

WebhookDeliveryStatus.description:
`pending` (queued or between retries), `delivered`, `failed` (retries exhausted),
`expired` (past `expires_at`), `cancelled` (the endpoint was disabled or deleted) or
`shadow` (recorded while the event type was held back, never sent).

WebhookEndpoint.description: A webhook endpoint. It never carries the signing secret: create and rotate-secret return it once.

api_version.description: The payload version this endpoint's deliveries carry.

failing_since.description: When the current run of failures began (ISO 8601), or null.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: While set, deliveries also carry a v1 signature made with the previous secret, until this time (ISO 8601).

secret_hint.description: The last 4 characters of the current signing secret, to tell secrets apart.

status_reason.description: Why the endpoint is not enabled, or null.

WebhookEndpointStatus.description:
`enabled`; `disabled` (by you, or after your receiver answered 410 Gone); or
`auto_disabled` (after 50 failed deliveries in a row and 3 days without a success). An
update with `enabled` set to true resumes a disabled or auto-disabled endpoint.

WebhookEndpointWithSecret.description: What create returns: the endpoint and its signing secret.

api_version.description: The payload version this endpoint's deliveries carry.

failing_since.description: When the current run of failures began (ISO 8601), or null.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: While set, deliveries also carry a v1 signature made with the previous secret, until this time (ISO 8601).

secret.description: The signing secret, `whsec_...`. Returned once: store it now.

secret_hint.description: The last 4 characters of the current signing secret, to tell secrets apart.

status_reason.description: Why the endpoint is not enabled, or null.

WebhookEvFoundData.description: `ev.found` data: a price on the EV board became tradeable at or above your `min_ev`.

board_age_ms.description: The EV board's age in milliseconds when the event was made, or null.

event_id.description: Our stable id of the game (`{sport}:{away}@{home}-{date}`), the `eventId` the odds board and the history endpoints use; empty when unknown.

odds_event_id.description: The game's `id` on the odds board: what the EV endpoint returns as `eventId`.

endpoint_id.description: The endpoint it was sent to, `whk_...`.

expires_at.description: No delivery is attempted after this (ISO 8601).

id.description: The event id, `evt_...`: identical on every retry and in the `Owls-Webhook-Id` header. Dedupe on it.

occurred_at.description: When what it reports happened, as far as is known (ISO 8601).

type.description: The event type; a type added later arrives as a string this version does not list.

WebhookEvFoundFilters.description: `ev.found` filters as stored: every field is set.

kinds.description: The price kinds that fire (default both).

min_ev.description: The least EV that fires, in percent: 1, 2, 3, 5 or 8 (default 3).

venues.description: Sportsbook or venue keys; empty (the default) means every one the EV board scores.

WebhookEvFoundFiltersInput.description: `ev.found` filters as sent: an omitted field keeps its default (create) or its stored value (update).

venues.description: Keys the EV board scores; a key that can never produce an event is refused with a 400.

WebhookEvKind.description: `ev.found` price kinds: `book` (a sportsbook) or `venue` (an exchange or prediction market).

WebhookEvSignal.description: The price behind an `ev.found` event, scored like the EV endpoint scores it.

ev.description: The EV in dollars: per $1 staked at a sportsbook, per contract at a venue. Null when it is not scored.

ev_percent.description: The EV in percent of the amount at risk, rounded to 2 decimals.

fair_low.description: The conservative fair (the fair less 1 percentage point) the EV is scored against, or null.

fair_probability.description: The fair probability of this side, or null.

fee.description: A venue's taker fee per contract, in dollars; 0 for a sportsbook.

link.description: The venue's page for the market, or null.

price.description: American odds of the price you pay (a venue's ask).

quote_age_ms.description: The price's age in milliseconds when the EV board was built, or null.

route.description: A venue's route: `yes`, or `no:<CODE>` (buy NO on the opponent's market); null for a sportsbook.

size.description: Dollars available at `price`, or null when unknown.

WebhookEventType.description: Every event type a delivery can carry: the subscribable ones and `webhook.test` (sent only on request, by the test call).

WebhookFilters.description: An endpoint's filters as stored: the API fills in every default.

sports.description: Sport keys; empty (the default) means every sport each subscribed event type covers.

WebhookFiltersInput.description:
Filters as sent. On create, an omitted field takes its default. On update they merge
into the stored filters: a section you send (`line_moved`, `ev_found`) changes only the
fields you send, and `sports` replaces the list (`[]` means every covered sport). A sport
that one of the endpoint's event types does not cover is refused with a 400
(`sport_not_covered`).

event_id.description: The game's id in the live scores.

score.description: Null when the scores show none.

endpoint_id.description: The endpoint it was sent to, `whk_...`.

expires_at.description: No delivery is attempted after this (ISO 8601).

id.description: The event id, `evt_...`: identical on every retry and in the `Owls-Webhook-Id` header. Dedupe on it.

occurred_at.description: When what it reports happened, as far as is known (ISO 8601).

type.description: The event type; a type added later arrives as a string this version does not list.

WebhookGameScore.description: A game's score. For tennis, sets won.

endpoint_id.description: The endpoint it was sent to, `whk_...`.

expires_at.description: No delivery is attempted after this (ISO 8601).

id.description: The event id, `evt_...`: identical on every retry and in the `Owls-Webhook-Id` header. Dedupe on it.

occurred_at.description: When what it reports happened, as far as is known (ISO 8601).

type.description: The event type; a type added later arrives as a string this version does not list.

WebhookGameStatus.description: A game's status as the live scores show it.

detail.description: Its detail text, such as the clock or the result.

state.description: The scores feed's state, such as `in` or `post`.

WebhookLineMovedData.description:
`line.moved` data: Pinnacle's main moneyline, spread or total for a game that has not
started moved by at least your step since the last `line.moved` you were sent for that
market, so small moves add up.

commence_time.description: The scheduled start (ISO 8601); empty when unknown.

event_id.description: Our stable id of the game (`{sport}:{away}@{home}-{date}`), the `eventId` the odds board and the history endpoints use. Empty when unknown.

max_probability_change_pp.description: The largest change of a side's implied probability from `previous`, in percentage points.

At least one of eventId, player or startDate is required; sport alone is rejected as too broad.

A player search that matches an unusually large number of distinct names is treated as a scan and served through a slower fallback with a tighter timeout.

The line and the prices live under `closing`, not at the top level of the row, and the player field is `playerName`. `opening` is present only on rows where an opening line was also captured, so treat it as optional.

A row carries EITHER a labelled pair or a single unlabelled price. `overPrice` and `underPrice` are set when the source stated which side each price belongs to. `americanPrice` is set when it published one price without naming a side. So null side prices mean the row was published one-way, NOT that the price is missing: on one NBA event of 1,133 rows, every row carried a price and 1,057 of them carried it as `americanPrice`.

Do not compare a one-way `americanPrice` against a two-way line as though they were quoted the same way. A two-way market splits its margin across both sides while a single published price carries all of it, so the one-way number reads shorter than a two-way line at a comparable number.

One row is one rung of the book ladder. `isMain` is true for the line the book was actually leading with, false for an alternate rung, and null where it is not known for that row. Null is not a hint that it was an alternate: older rows predate the distinction and it cannot be recovered, so filter on `isMain === true` when you want main lines only and expect null rows to be excluded.

An alternate rung carries one price in `americanPrice` and nothing in the side fields, and it reflects the ladder as it stood at the last pre-game capture, so it has no opening of its own. Only the main line carries open-to-close movement.

CHECK `closing.capturedAt` BEFORE TREATING THESE AS CLOSING NUMBERS. A main line is the last quote we hold with BOTH sides priced, and books commonly go one-way as tip approaches, so the two-way number can predate the game by hours. Measured on one NBA game, the median gap between the last quote of any kind and the last two-sided one was 187 minutes. The price is real, it is simply not always recent, and capturedAt is how you tell.

Returns live games across every supported sport in one call, with current score, period and status.

Score changes for games in play are also pushed on the scores-update WebSocket event, opt-in with scores in the subscription, using this endpoint's event ids. That event carries a lean view (status with the clock, teams, score); this endpoint has the full event. A push fires when the score, the state, the period or the running flag of the clock changes, never on every clock tick.

503 until the first scoreboard has been collected.

NFL, NCAAF and NBA give the period in status.period and its label in status.detail: Q1 to Q4, Halftime (period 2), or OT (period 5 for every overtime; overtimes are not numbered). NHL gives P1 to P3, Intermission between periods (around the restart, status.period can already be the next period), OT (period 4 for every overtime) or SO (period 5). While one of these games is in play, status.displayClock is the time left in the period as the venue shows it (5:32, or 48.3 under a minute) and status.clock carries it as secondsRemaining with running (true while it runs, false in a stoppage or intermission, null when the feed cannot say: NFL and NCAAF between plays, and any game before its first movement is seen), intermission (halftime or between periods), period and asOf, the instant the clock was read: tick secondsRemaining down from asOf locally while running. The clock is read every few seconds and is absent when none was read for the game. Soccer status.detail is the half (1st Half, 2nd Half) and the match minute is status.displayClock, e.g. 67 or 45+2. A phase without a label, soccer half-time included, reads Live with status.period null, as does college basketball. MLB gives the inning in status.period and status.detail (e.g. Top 7th); in extra innings status.detail reads Top Extra Inning, Bot Extra Inning, or Extra Inning when the half is unknown, with status.period null, because extra innings are not numbered. On /scores/live, a baseball linescore period 10 is every extra inning combined.

post.description:
Registers an HTTPS endpoint for signed event notifications: Pinnacle line moves, positive EV prices, game start and final, and graded player props. Returns the signing secret once.

Coverage by event type (a sport listed in filters.sports that one of your event types does not cover is a 400): line.moved: mlb, nba, ncaab, ncaaf, nfl, nhl, soccer, tennis, wnba; ev.found: cs2, dota2, lol, mlb, mma, nba, ncaab, ncaaf, nfl, nhl, soccer, tennis, valorant, wnba; game.started: mlb, nba, ncaab, nhl, soccer, tennis, nfl, ncaaf; game.final: mlb, nba, ncaab, nhl, soccer, tennis, nfl, ncaaf; props.graded: mlb, nfl.

line.moved: Pinnacle's main moneyline, spread or total for a game that has not started moved by at least your step since the last line.moved you were sent for that market, so small moves add up. price_step_pp is the change in implied probability in percentage points (0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5), point_step the change in the spread or total line (0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3). A line change smaller than point_step restarts the price comparison at the new line. After a line.moved the market is quiet for 60 seconds, and a move inside that window is sent once at its end if it still clears your step. data: { sport, league, event_id, source_event_id, home_team, away_team, commence_time, book, market, reason, previous, current, max_probability_change_pp, point_change, thresholds }, where previous and current map each side (home, away, draw, over, under) to { price, point }.

ev.found: a price on the EV board became tradeable at or above your min_ev, in percent (1, 2, 3, 5, 8), by the same fair-value math as the EV endpoint. Tradeable means it clears the trade bar: a sportsbook price needs an EV of at least 2%; an exchange or prediction-market price needs at least 4% on its cost, a bid, a spread of 4 cents or less and $50 at the ask, so a min_ev below those floors adds nothing. It fires when the price crosses min_ev, again only after its EV has fallen more than 1 point below min_ev, or the price has been gone or stopped clearing the trade bar for two consecutive reads (about 40 seconds), and at most once per 15 minutes for one event, venue and side. After an alert, the same price for that event, venue and side is not sent again for 2 hours unless its EV has risen by at least 1 point. Nothing fires while the odds behind the board are out of date. kinds narrows to book (sportsbook) or venue (exchange and prediction market) prices; venues narrows to the listed keys, which must be among fanduel, draftkings, betmgm, bet365, caesars, kalshi, novig, 1xbet, betonline, betr, bovada (other keys can never produce an event, so they are refused). data: { sport, league, event_id, odds_event_id, home_team, away_team, commence_time, min_ev, signal: { kind, venue, side, team, price, implied_probability, fair_probability, fair_low, ev_percent, ev, fee, route, size, link, quote_age_ms }, board_age_ms }.

game.started: sent once per game when the live scores show it in play on two reads at least 15 seconds apart. game.final: sent once per game when they show it final on two reads at least 60 seconds apart and the final is believable: in tennis a player has won 2 sets, so a match that ends by retirement or walkover before that is not announced; in the other sports the game has run at least 80 minutes (soccer), 90 minutes (nba), 80 minutes (ncaab), 90 minutes (nhl), 90 minutes (mlb), 120 minutes (nfl), 150 minutes (ncaaf) from its start. A game reported final earlier than that, as an interrupted one can be, is not announced then; if the live scores show it in play again, its final is sent when it ends. A postponed or cancelled game never sends it. Status changes can trail the real moment by a few minutes. data: { sport, event_id, league, home_team, away_team, start_time, status: { state, detail }, score: { home, away } }; for tennis the score is sets won.

props.graded: sent when the first player prop results of a game are confirmed (complete: false) and again when every result of the game is confirmed (complete: true); a game confirmed in one pass sends a single event with complete: true. Games graded before you subscribed are not replayed, except that a game graded in the 30 minutes before can be, and a game graded during an interruption of the service longer than 30 minutes may not be announced. data: { sport, event_id, game_date, complete, confirmed_count, pending_count, results_path }; read the results from results_path.

Every delivery is a POST of the JSON { id, type, api_version, created, occurred_at, expires_at, endpoint_id, data } (api_version 2026-10-01) with the headers Owls-Webhook-Id (the event id), Owls-Event-Type, Owls-Delivery-Attempt and Owls-Signature.

Owls-Signature is t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with your signing secret (the whole string, whsec_ included, as UTF-8) over t, a period, and the raw request body, then compare it with v1 in constant time, and reject a t more than 5 minutes from your clock. The SDKs ship verifyWebhookSignature (TypeScript) and verify_webhook_signature (Python).

Delivery is at least once and unordered: dedupe on id, which is identical on every retry, and do not rely on one event arriving before another.

Answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds (3 to connect). Anything else is a failure, a redirect included: redirects are never followed. line.moved and ev.found retry after about 5 s, 20 s, 1 m and then expire; the other types retry after about 10 s, 1 m, 5 m, 15 m, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, 12 h. Retry-After is honoured. Nothing is sent after expires_at: line.moved 5 minutes, ev.found 2 minutes, game.started 2 hours, game.final 24 hours, props.graded 24 hours after the event.

410 Gone disables the endpoint. After 5 failures in a row its deliveries pause briefly (30 seconds, doubling up to 30 minutes). After 50 failures in a row and 72 hours without a success it is disabled (status auto_disabled); PATCH { "enabled": true } resumes it.

The url must be https on the default port with a public hostname. IP addresses, private or reserved addresses and internal hostnames are refused, at registration and on every delivery.

Endpoints per plan: MVP 3, Hall of Fame 10. Events per account: MVP 120 a minute and 20,000 a day, Hall of Fame 600 a minute and 100,000 a day; events over the cap are dropped, and so are new line.moved and ev.found events for an endpoint with more than 1,000 undelivered. At most 30 endpoint changes per minute per account.

get.description:
Returns positive expected value opportunities for a sport: for each event, the sportsbooks offering a moneyline price (or, with market, a spread or total price) that beats our fair price. The fair is Pinnacle's de-vigged line; the other books do not move it, they only block a side when they disagree with it by more than 1.5 points. EV is computed at the fair minus a 1-point safety margin, the same math as the public markets page.

fairProbability is the conservative fair: the fair minus 1 point. fairPrice, evPct, edgePp and kellyFraction are all computed at it, so for a sportsbook evPct = (fairProbability x decimal odds - 1) x 100. The fair before that margin is fairUnadjusted on each opportunity and fair.home / fair.away / fair.draw on each event.

Each sportsbook price is scored against a fair that leaves that book's own feed out, so a book never votes on its own price. Sportsbook prices are scored only when Pinnacle prices the game; exchange prices (Novig, and Kalshi and Polymarket with venues=true) can also be scored against the agreement of at least three independent books. booksInConsensus on an opportunity counts the independent sources behind the fair that price was scored against (1 means Pinnacle alone); on an event it counts the sources behind the event's fair.

tradeable is true when the opportunity clears the markets page trade bar (sportsbooks: EV of at least 2%; prediction markets: at least 4%, a bid, a spread of 4 cents or less and at least $50 at the ask); reason says why not. For a prediction market, evPct = (fairProbability - ask - fee) / (ask + fee) x 100.

No opportunity is listed while the odds snapshot behind the answer is over 90 seconds old, or for a game that has started. Within that, a sportsbook price must be under 3 minutes old and an exchange quote under 2 minutes, each by its own timestamp; quoteAgeMs is its age when the answer was served. meta.freshness and meta.board say how old the data is; with no data at all, meta.timestamp is 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z and meta.freshness.stale is true.

Pregame only; meta.market and meta.pregame_only state the market and this on every response.

With market=spreads or totals, each event is one game and market: point is the home number (spreads) or the total, and each opportunity carries its own point (the favourite's -3.5, the underdog's +3.5). fairProbability and fair are keyed home/away on spreads and over/under on totals. A book is compared only when it hangs exactly Pinnacle's number; nothing is converted between numbers, and there is no consensus fallback without a current Pinnacle line. venues does not apply: Kalshi and Polymarket are never scored on spreads or totals, and a Novig price is listed with kind venue and tradeable false (its depth is not checked here) and only while its quote is under 2 minutes old. A book whose own two-way price sits more than 10 points from Pinnacle's is treated as a different bet and is not scored. When meta.unsupported is set, nothing is scored for that sport and meta.freshness.stale is true.

On a whole number (pushPossible true) a push refunds the stake. The fair is the chance of each side given no push, so evPct is the EV of a bet that is not refunded: it can overstate the EV by the push chance and never flips its sign.

Tennis, esports and MMA return no spread or total opportunities (meta.unsupported says why): their books do not agree on what a handicap counts, for example sets against games.

Prices are American odds (meta.odds_format).

get.description:
Returns the Owls fair line for a sport: the fair moneyline, spread and total of every upcoming game Pinnacle prices, each side as a probability and as American odds. The fair is Pinnacle's de-vigged line; other books only flag a side when they disagree with it by more than 1.5 points. Use it to price any bet yourself, including games where no book offers positive EV.

These are the fairs before the 1-point safety margin /ev scores against. Each side is the lower of two de-vig models (multiplicative and power), so the sides of one market add up to at most 1, and slightly under whenever the two models differ.

A game with no current fair on any market is left out. A market is null when there is no current fair for it: no Pinnacle line for that market, or its data is too old (meta.boards says which). The moneyline can also come from the agreement of at least three independent books when Pinnacle has no line (method consensus); spreads and totals never do. Sports and games Pinnacle does not price (for example most esports and MMA cards) usually return no fair.

Spreads and totals are priced at Pinnacle's main number. On a whole number (pushPossible true) the fair is the chance of each side given no push.

Spreads and totals are supported for nba, ncaab, nfl, ncaaf, nhl, mlb, wnba and soccer (meta.markets); other sports return the moneyline only.

Pregame only: a game leaves the list when it starts.
