get.description:
Returns player injury designations for a sport from two independent sources, each attributed and separately timestamped, plus a derived consensus where the sources can be matched to the same player with confidence.

Supported sports are nfl and mlb. Other sports return 404.

Every player carries one record per source that covers them, with that source own status, detail and report time. Records are never merged into one another.

record.source is a role label, either primary or secondary, and meta.sources is keyed the same way. It identifies which of the sport two feeds a record came from so you can tell them apart and prefer one consistently. It is stable if a feed is changed underneath it.

consensus is present only when the two sources can be matched to the same player with confidence. When they disagree, consensus.agreement is conflict and consensus.injuryStatus is null, and both records are returned.

Players whose identity could not be established are listed in meta.unresolvedIdentity and carry no consensus. That includes a player whose two spellings differ only by a suffix when nothing else corroborates that they are the same person, since adding a suffix to one of two players is how a league separates a shared name.

consensus.listDaysConflict is true when both sources agree a player is on an injured list but disagree about its length, for example 10 days against 60. The designation still reads as agreeing, so check this flag when the length matters.

meta.sources[source].ageSeconds is null when the age is unknown, and is never 0 as a placeholder. A source is marked stale when its age is unknown, when it is older than 30 minutes, or when it holds no records.

meta.sources[source].checks names the validations that ran on that source own data. Checks are reported per source, never pooled, so one source never inherits another.

Cleared and roster-move designations are excluded by default. Pass includeActive=true to receive them, or name them explicitly in status, which overrides the default view.

There are two clocks and they answer different questions. meta.sources[source].ageSeconds is how long ago we fetched the feed. record.reportAgeSeconds is how long ago that source published the designation itself, which is the one that tells you whether a status is current.

record.reportAgeSeconds is null when a source publishes no timestamp of its own, and is never 0 as a placeholder. player.reportAge counts how many of a player records could be dated and how many could not, so a partly dated player is visible as such.

consensus.stale is true when every dated record behind a designation is older than consensus.staleAfterSeconds, false when at least one is inside it, and null when no verdict is possible. Null is never a substitute for false.

There are two reasons stale can be null, and staleAfterSeconds tells them apart. A number beside a null stale means the rule exists but nothing carried a timestamp to judge against it. A null staleAfterSeconds means no rule applies at all, for one of four reasons: the designation is one whose currency does not decay, such as active or a status we could not map; the sources disagree about the designation; they disagree about the length of an injured list stint; or a season ending placement does not expire. The first of those covers most players on a response that includes cleared designations.

The staleness window depends on the designation, not only the sport. A weekly football designation such as questionable lapses after 10 days because the injury report is reissued every game week, while a baseball injured-list placement is given its own stint length plus two weeks, and a season-ending placement is never marked stale.

meta.reportAgeSummary describes this response. staleConsensus, freshConsensus, noVerdict and noConsensus partition the players returned and add up to count. playersWithNoDatedRecord, datedRecords and undatedRecords say how much of the whole response could be dated, and are not scoped to any of those four buckets.

A source that publishes no timestamps of its own yields no staleness verdict for a player only it covers, so filtering with source can return a page on which every consensus.stale is null.

Records are retained by the source after a season ends, so check reportedAt and reportAgeSeconds on each record.

503 until the first collection has completed.

get.description:
Returns the play-by-play of one NBA, NHL, NFL, NCAAF or soccer game in play (or ended within the last 6 hours), oldest play first, or without eventId the list of games that have play-by-play. For soccer the plays are the match incidents: goals, own goals, penalties, cards and substitutions.

eventId is the id GET /api/v1/{sport}/scores/live gives the game. Play-by-play exists while a game is in play and for 6 hours after it ends; before tip-off, and for any other id, the response is 404 with a hint. Without eventId the response lists the games that have play-by-play, with their state and play count.

Each play carries the source's own id and order (seq, ascending, not contiguous), the period and the time left in it (clock as the venue shows it, secondsRemaining), team (home or away: the offense, the shooter's team, the team that committed the penalty; null for a neutral play such as a period start), type (the source's own type key, unchanged: NFL and NCAAF Rush, Pass Reception, Punt, Field Goal Good; NHL shot-on-goal, faceoff, hit, penalty, goal; NBA 2pt/Jump Shot, rebound/defensive, turnover/bad pass, freethrow/1 of 2), text, scoringPlay, the score after the play (homeScore, awayScore), wallclock (when the play happened per the source; null for the NHL, which publishes none) and detail, the sport's own fields.

detail for NFL and NCAAF: drive, down, distance, yardLine, yardsToEndzone, downDistanceText, possessionText before the play, endDown, endDistance, endYardLine, endYardsToEndzone, endDownDistanceText after it, yards, scoreValue, isPenalty, isTurnover. For the NHL: situationCode (skaters and goalies on the ice, the league's code), zone, x, y, shotType, reason, penalty {descKey, typeCode, duration}, players [{role, id, name, sweater}] with the roles scorer, assist, shooter, goalie, winner, loser, hitter, hittee, blocker, player, committedBy, drawnBy, servedBy, and homeShotsOnGoal and awayShotsOnGoal on shots; the NHL feed scores only goal plays, so every other play carries the running tally. For the NBA: subType, descriptor, qualifiers, playerId, playerName, teamTricode, shotResult (Made or Missed), shotDistance (feet), x, y, isFieldGoal, possession. For soccer: minute, addedMinutes (stoppage time, e.g. 2 for 45+2), player {id, name}, assist (on a goal), playerOut (on a substitution, whose player is the one coming on), card (yellow, red or yellow-red), note, code; clock is the match minute as shown (45+2), seq is derived from the period and minute (the source has no sequence of its own, so an inserted or withdrawn incident renumbers only the plays of its own minute), secondsRemaining and wallclock are null, period is the half (1, 2; 3 and 4 extra time; 5 penalties), type is the incident label (Goal, Own goal, Penalty, Yellow Card, Red Card, Substitution) and team the side credited with it, the scoring side on an own goal; every soccer game on /scores/live is covered, whatever its league.

A play can be amended after it is first published (a review, an assist added, a scorer corrected), so merge plays by id; each play's updatedAt is when its current content was first seen. since=<seq> returns the plays after that seq plus any play amended in the last 2 minutes whatever its seq (meta.amendedWindowSeconds), so a poller that passes the lastSeq it has every two minutes or sooner sees every amendment; limit=<n> returns the last n plays, applied after since. A since or limit that is not an integer in range is a 400. meta.returned and meta.truncated say what the filters did.

meta.asOf is when the source was read and meta.ageSeconds how long ago that was; status is stale when a game in play has not been read for 30 seconds (the reader runs every few seconds). meta.sourceAgeSeconds is the source's own edge-cache age at that read, null when it sends none: NHL plays can be up to about 20 seconds behind the ice, NFL and NCAAF plays about 7 seconds, NBA plays are not cached. Soccer incidents are read every 20 seconds per match and at once when the match score changes, so a goal shows within a few seconds and a card or substitution within about 20; a soccer game is stale after 60 seconds without a read.

The same plays are pushed on the plays-update WebSocket event, opt-in with plays in the subscription (true, or an array of nba, nhl, nfl, ncaaf, soccer), same access as scores-update: one message per sport within a few seconds of a new play, carrying only the plays new or amended since the previous message.

get.description:
Returns the fair line and positive expected value prices for player props: for each upcoming prop Pinnacle prices both ways, the fair over and under with the vig removed, and every sportsbook price at the same player, stat and line that beats it. The same math as the moneyline /ev: Pinnacle anchors the fair, the other books only flag a side they disagree with by more than 1.5 points, and EV is computed at the fair minus a 1-point margin.

A price is compared only at the same player, the same category and exactly the same line. Only half lines (x.5) are priced: on a whole line, over 20 and 20+ settle differently at exactly 20. Props naming several players are left out.

fairProbability on an opportunity is the conservative fair (the fair minus 1 point), and evPct = (fairProbability x decimal odds - 1) x 100. fair.over and fair.under are the fairs before that margin; each side is the lower of two de-vig models, so they add up to at most 1.

fair.over.booksDisagree / fair.under.booksDisagree count every book; each opportunity is scored against a fair that leaves its own book out, so a price from the one book that disagrees can still be listed (and tradeable).

A one-sided price (an anytime touchdown with no under, for example) is scored on its side. A book whose own two-way price sits more than 10 points from Pinnacle's is treated as a different bet and is never listed.

Novig is listed with kind venue and tradeable false: its depth, bid and spread are not checked on props. Kalshi and Polymarket are not scored here.

Props whose category no mapper could name, and a player key two differently named players share in one game (Luis Garcia and Luis Garcia Jr., for example), are left out. So is a one-sided price whose implied probability sits more than 10 points from Pinnacle's fair on that side.

Pinnacle must have priced the prop within the last 3 minutes, and a sportsbook price must be under 3 minutes old (Novig under 2), each by its own timestamp. A prop Pinnacle has pulled is not listed. Started games are left out.

Supported for nba, ncaab, wnba, nfl, ncaaf, nhl, mlb and soccer.

status on each entry is ok, dnp, no_stats, unmapped_category or stat_not_reported. An entry or line that could not be graded carries ungradableReason: dnp (the bet voids), no_stats (no box-score row matched, never treated as a void), stat_not_reported, unmapped_category, ungradable_structure (an integer line whose over/under versus N+ meaning is unknown), ambiguous_player (a display name shared by two players in the game, so no line is joined) or no_actual_value.

verdict on a line is over, under or push for an over/under market and hit or miss for a milestone (N+) market. A book's market structure is honoured when it published one; an absent structure is unknown and is never defaulted to over/under.

capturePhase archive marks the last in-play line, captured at game end because the pre-game close was missed. It is not a closing line, and a hit rate built on it is not comparable to one built on commence lines.

Provisional grades are included by default and every entry carries final; meta.provisional counts them. Box scores are revised for a short window after a game, so confirmed_only=true trades some delay for a grade read after that window. A stat correction published later can still change a confirmed grade.

meta.lineOutcomes counts verdicts per book line; meta.entryStatuses counts entries per player and category. They have different denominators, so a hit rate built from lineOutcomes is weighted by how many books quoted each player.

Grading is enabled sport by sport and runs after the game is final and the box score is published. Until then, or on a sport where grading is not enabled, data is empty and meta.message says so.

meta.checks lists exactly what was evaluated. The response never claims a game is fully graded.

get.description:
Returns real-time Pinnacle odds for a sport. For the esports keys (cs2, lol, valorant, dota2) the response is the Pinnacle wire format unchanged and league is required; every other sport returns the normalized realtime event shape.

meta.source names the real-time feed that answered; meta.available is false and meta.freshness.stale is true whenever the response is empty.

meta.feed.lastDataAgeSeconds is the time since this sport last produced any data, or null if it never has; it is the field to watch for a feed that has stopped. For a feed that is running but hearing nothing from Pinnacle, watch meta.feed.upstreamAgeSeconds.

meta.feed.upstreamAgeSeconds is the time since Pinnacle last sent anything for this sport, and meta.feed.resubscribing is true while the feed is subscribing again after a reconnect, when some leagues can be silent. lastDataAgeSeconds stays low while Pinnacle is quiet, because the board is rewritten on a schedule either way; upstreamAgeSeconds keeps growing. Both are null when unknown, which includes every response whose meta.source is not pinnacle and the moments before the feed has received anything since it started.

meta.feed.stalled is true when the board has an event in play (phase live) and Pinnacle has sent nothing for this sport for longer than its normal quiet spells during play (5 minutes for NFL and college football, 8 for soccer and MLB, 12 for tennis and WNBA, 18 for NHL and every other sport): prices can be out of date even though the board was rewritten seconds ago. It is false on a board with nothing in play, however quiet, and null when upstreamAgeSeconds is null or the events carry no phase. It does not change meta.freshness.stale. The pinnacle-realtime WebSocket event carries the same field in its feed object.

Each event carries status and isLive and may carry phase: scheduled (not started), live (in play, betting open), suspended (in play, betting paused for now; its markets carry suspended: true) or closed (betting over for good; the event is sent that way for a few minutes, then removed). phase can gain values, so treat an unknown one like a missing field. When phase is present, isLive is true while in-play betting on the match is running. Without phase, isLive can be false on a match that is in progress, so check status as well, and read phase first whenever it is present.

A main market (moneyline, spread, total or team total) that Pinnacle takes down while the rest of the match stays open also carries suspended: true, and loses it when Pinnacle offers it again or its period ends. On a spread or total the flag is on the main line only; its alternateLines are not flagged one by one, so read each rung's last_seen for those.

When meta.source is pinnacle, each event also carries lastUpdate and seenAt (epoch milliseconds) and freshness: { lastUpdate, ageSeconds, stale, refreshedAt, refreshedAgeSeconds }. freshness.lastUpdate is the price change the event's freshness is measured from and ageSeconds its age; refreshedAt is the last time the feed confirmed a price on the event, changed or not, and refreshedAgeSeconds its age. stale is true when the event reads as in play and ageSeconds is over 30 or unknown; pre-match prices can sit unchanged for hours and are not flagged. The event-level lastUpdate can be older than the newest price on an in-play event, so for the age of one market read that market's last_update.

markets[].last_update is when that market's price last changed, and last_seen, where present, when the feed last confirmed it. That holds for the main lines: h2h, spreads, totals, team_totals, total_games, and their corner, first_half_ and set versions. On special_ markets folded from a sub-matchup, on btts markets and on the other markets, last_update moves with the whole matchup or sub-matchup rather than the single market, so do not read it as that market's own age.

Each alternateLines rung (point and price) may carry its own last_seen, when the feed last confirmed that rung. Pinnacle does not resend every rung in every message, so a rung whose last_seen is well behind its market's is a hint that Pinnacle has taken it down, not proof.

meta.stream is { epoch, seq }, the position on the pinnacle-realtime stream that this response matches, or null when the response cannot be aligned with the stream. To follow pinnacle-realtime without gaps, wait up to 25 seconds for a frame whose stream.checkpoint is true (call at once if the frames carry no stream), then call this endpoint. If meta.stream is null, replace your board with data, apply every frame, and call again after 10, 20, 40 seconds and so on, up to every 5 minutes. If its epoch differs from the checkpoint's, or its seq is lower than the checkpoint's, call again at the next checkpoint. Otherwise replace your board with data and apply only frames with a seq above meta.stream.seq, in order; a skipped seq or a new epoch after that means calling again. The pinnacle-realtime event description has the full procedure.

When meta.stream is set, data is the board at that position after the league filter and the filters this endpoint applies to every response (confirmed finished events, events too old to still be live, duplicates), so an empty data array means no event matches, not a missing feed.

meta.freshness.droppedAsFinished and droppedAsStale count events removed because they were confirmed finished or their start time is too far past to still be live.

Esports rows each carry their own freshness; the top-level freshness is the freshest served event and stale is true only when no served event is fresh.

The SDK exposes the esports keys through getEsportsRealtime / get_esports_realtime, which enforce the league parameter.

Soccer women's and youth leagues: Pinnacle names the clubs as in the senior league and puts Women or the age only in the league label. The team names here carry that marker (Liverpool Women, Uzbekistan U23), and so does every outcome label that names a team, such as Draw No Bet, Double Chance (Draw Or Uzbekistan U23) and progression outrights. The v2 Pinnacle endpoints keep Pinnacle's own names.

Returns live games for one sport with current score, period and status.

Score changes for games in play are also pushed on the scores-update WebSocket event, opt-in with scores in the subscription, using this endpoint's event ids. That event carries a lean view (status with the clock, teams, score); this endpoint has the full event. A push fires when the score, the state, the period or the running flag of the clock changes, never on every clock tick.

An empty events array with hasScheduledGames true means games are scheduled but none has started.

NFL, NCAAF and NBA give the period in status.period and its label in status.detail: Q1 to Q4, Halftime (period 2), or OT (period 5 for every overtime; overtimes are not numbered). NHL gives P1 to P3, Intermission between periods (around the restart, status.period can already be the next period), OT (period 4 for every overtime) or SO (period 5). While one of these games is in play, status.displayClock is the time left in the period as the venue shows it (5:32, or 48.3 under a minute) and status.clock carries it as secondsRemaining with running (true while it runs, false in a stoppage or intermission, null when the feed cannot say: NFL and NCAAF between plays, and any game before its first movement is seen), intermission (halftime or between periods), period and asOf, the instant the clock was read: tick secondsRemaining down from asOf locally while running. The clock is read every few seconds and is absent when none was read for the game. Soccer status.detail is the half (1st Half, 2nd Half) and the match minute is status.displayClock, e.g. 67 or 45+2. A phase without a label, soccer half-time included, reads Live with status.period null, as does college basketball. MLB gives the inning in status.period and status.detail (e.g. Top 7th); in extra innings status.detail reads Top Extra Inning, Bot Extra Inning, or Extra Inning when the half is unknown, with status.period null, because extra innings are not numbered. On /scores/live, a baseball linescore period 10 is every extra inning combined.

post.description:
Prices several same game parlays in one call: each on one book (mode book) or each on every same game parlay book (mode compare). Each book's answer is exactly what /sgp/build returns for that book and parlay.

Parlays are priced one after the other, in request order; in mode compare the books price each parlay side by side, as on /sgp/compare. A parlay whose pricing would begin more than about 20 seconds after the call began has status not-started and was not priced, except for any book answered from a cached quote, and carries no fair block: send it again. A slow book prices fewer parlays in that time (FanDuel takes about 5 to 15 seconds a parlay). Every other parlay has status done. bookStatus (mode book) and books[].status (mode compare) take the values /sgp/compare uses: priced, refused, unresolved, busy, no-price, timeout, event-not-listed, ambiguous-event, unsupported, disabled or skipped.

A parlay repeated in one batch (same eventId, same legs in the same order) is priced once and reported for each copy.

Before a game starts, a book that priced exactly these legs for this game in the last 15 seconds may be answered from that quote, as on /sgp/compare: cached is true, result.meta.cached is true and result.meta.cacheAgeMs is the quote's age when the response was sent; result.meta.pricedAt is still when the book priced it. A cached answer costs no build. Send fresh: true to price everything now. A game that starts within a minute is always priced fresh.

Every quote not answered from a cached quote counts one build against your per-minute SGP build limit (one per parlay in mode book, one per book and parlay in mode compare), reserved for the whole batch before any book is priced. A quote that never reaches the book (not listed, a different game, a leg that does not resolve, no time left, or a parlay not started) is given back at once while the minute it was counted in is still running. Over the limit the call is a 429 SGP_RATE_LIMIT with unitsNeeded and a Retry-After header; a batch that needs more builds than your limit allows at all is a 429 SGP_BATCH_TOO_LARGE with unitsNeeded and no Retry-After. A batch counts as one request against your plan rate limit.

In mode book, a book outside the SGP books is a 400 SGP_BOOK_UNSUPPORTED, a book that does not price the sport a 400 SGP_BOOK_SPORT_UNSUPPORTED, and a book whose pricing is paused a 503 SGP_BOOK_DISABLED, as on /sgp/build.

MVP and Hall of Fame plans. On a lower plan the call is a 403 with code SGP_TIER_REQUIRED; a 503 with code SGP_FEATURE_DISABLED means batches are not switched on yet.

post.description:
Prices a same game parlay on the book named in book (FanDuel, DraftKings, Hard Rock, BetRivers, Bally Bet and BetMGM): resolves each leg to that book's own selection for one game and returns that book's own correlation-adjusted same game parlay price for exactly those legs, verified leg by leg, not a naive multiplication of the singles.

The price is the named book's own same game parlay price for exactly the legs sent, at the lines they resolved to, verified leg by leg: it is returned only when the book's answer confirms all of that; otherwise the call fails rather than returning a price. On a 200, sgp.isSGM is always true. A book whose pricing misbehaves may be paused: its builds are then a 503 SGP_BOOK_DISABLED until it is switched back on, and the other books are unaffected.

A resolved leg carries the book's own ids: fdSelection { marketId, selectionId } on FanDuel, bookSelection { marketId, selectionId } on every other book (DraftKings: its market id and selection id; Hard Rock: its market id and selection id, both strings of digits; BetRivers and Bally Bet: the book's offer id and outcome id, both strings of digits; BetMGM: marketId v1:<fixture>:<market> or v2:<fixture>:<market>, which names the BetMGM platform, fixture and market the pick is sent with, and selectionId its option id; on NHL, marketId sc:<fixture>:<builder id> and selectionId the option string BetMGM's bet builder lists for it). Only one of the two is present on a leg.

FanDuel prices are FanDuel's own bet-slip price, quoted from FanDuel's New Jersey sportsbook. FanDuel runs separate markets in other states and in Ontario, so a slip placed there can show a different parlay price for the same legs. The price also moves with the market, so compare it only with a slip taken at the time in meta.pricedAt.

fdSelection.marketId is FanDuel New Jersey's id for that market. FanDuel issues a different marketId in every other state and in Ontario, while selectionId is the same everywhere, so to place a leg outside New Jersey use your region's marketId for that selectionId.

meta.timestamp and meta.resolvedAt are the same instant: when the legs were resolved against the book's catalog, BEFORE pricing. meta.catalogAgeMs is the MINIMUM age that catalog data already had then; the true age can be higher. meta.priceRequestedAt is when the price request went out and meta.pricedAt is when the book's answer came back, both on our server's clock. Each can read slightly LATER than the real moment, by the time the answer took to reach our server (typically under 100 ms). If that timing detail is unavailable, priceRequestedAt is when pricing started (earlier than the request) and pricedAt is when the answer reached our server, so the two still enclose the quote. pricedAt is never earlier than priceRequestedAt and is the quote time to use. They are present on every 200, and on a refused 422 or a no-price 503 only when the book returned a response. catalogAgeMs is omitted when the age is unknown.

422 with reasonCode "unresolved" (code repeats it) when any leg cannot be resolved on the book, including a selection the book has suspended; the legs array says which leg and why. Nothing was priced.

422 also when two legs resolve to the same selection on the book, and on FanDuel for player props whose line is carried only in the selection name, because FanDuel does not confirm that line in its price response. These are refused before pricing.

On FanDuel, alternate N-or-more strikeout rungs are priced, but its price response identifies the rung by its selection only and does not confirm its line. A 200 that includes one carries meta.lineUnverified: true and meta.lineUnverifiedLegs, the indexes of those legs in your legs array. On BetMGM NHL, the price response names no leg at all, so every NHL leg is listed there. Both keys are absent when every line was confirmed, and never appear on a DraftKings, Hard Rock, BetRivers or Bally Bet build, or a BetMGM NFL or NBA build, because each confirms every line.

Player prop coverage is not uniform across books, sports and categories. The categories a player_prop leg can use on FanDuel, per sport: mlb: strikeouts, hits, total-bases, home-runs, rbis, runs, stolen-bases, singles, doubles, triples, hits-runs-rbis. nba: accepted: points, rebounds, assists, threes, steals, blocks. wnba: points, rebounds, and accepted: assists, threes, steals, blocks. nfl: touchdowns, passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, receptions, passing_tds, and accepted: first_touchdown_scorer. nhl: goals, hockey_points, hockey_assists, shots_on_goal, first_goal_scorer. ncaaf, ncaab, soccer and tennis have no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused before pricing, with the reason in legs[].reason, when it has not. Football, basketball and hockey categories use the /props category names (receptions, points, hockey_points; for NHL, points and assists are accepted too), except basketball threes, which /props calls threes_made; baseball categories use the builder's MLB names (strikeouts, total-bases). A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: mlb, nba, wnba, nfl, ncaaf, nhl and ncaab: moneyline, spread and total; soccer and tennis: moneyline only. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

Spread and total legs price at the book's main line. On NHL, Hard Rock, Bally Bet and, before the game, DraftKings also price an alternate puck line or total they list: send the point you want, and a point the book does not list is refused naming the lines it lists. team_total legs price on Hard Rock NHL only. Every other book and sport refuses an alternate point (Hard Rock, DraftKings, BetMGM, BetRivers and Bally Bet name their main line in the reason; FanDuel names only the point it could not find), and refuses a team_total leg as a leg type it does not price. Alternate lines and team_total legs can be switched off: while they are, an alternate point is refused naming the book's main line, and a team_total leg is a 400 as an unknown leg type.

A leg with a period (P1, P2 or P3, NHL) prices on Hard Rock only: a period moneyline is that period's 3-way result (a team, or Tie for a tied period), and a period spread or total prices at a line Hard Rock lists for that period (before the game, Hard Rock lists a total and a spread for the 1st period). Every other book refuses a leg with a period as unsupported; no book ever prices it as the full game. Period legs can be switched off, and while they are, a leg with a period is refused the same way. There is no regulation-time leg: Hard Rock does not combine its regulation result with other legs. A period that is not P1, P2 or P3, a period on a sport other than NHL, and a period on a team_total or player_prop leg are a 400.

fair: true (MVP and Hall of Fame plans) adds fair, our estimate of the parlay's price built from de-vigged leg probabilities. It is never the book's price: sgp is unchanged, and fair.estimate is always true. Each leg's probability is our Fair v1 fair: for moneylines, spreads and totals the fair /api/v1/{sport}/fair serves (a spread or total only at that fair's own number, never a whole number), for player props the fair /api/v1/{sport}/props/ev scores against (x.5 lines). Each leg's source says whether Pinnacle anchored it or, for a moneyline, at least three books agreed; booksDisagree flags a leg other books price differently. The legs' probabilities are multiplied and adjusted by how the book itself priced these legs together: basis.correlationFactor is the product of the book's single prices divided by its parlay price. That factor also keeps the book's parlay surcharge over its singles (basis.marginAdjusted is false), so the estimate removes the singles' vig, not that surcharge. fair.price is null, with fair.why, when any leg has no fair (coverage.missingLegs and each leg's why say which, for example a line off the fair's number or a fair board too old to use), when the book returned no single price for a leg (BetMGM NHL returns none) or a factor outside 0.25 to 4, once the game has started, or when the fair could not be worked out in time. fair.independent is the same legs treated as unrelated. fair is added to priced 200s only. On a Rookie plan, fair: true is a 403 with code SGP_TIER_REQUIRED, sent before anything is priced and not counted against any limit; a 503 with code SGP_FEATURE_DISABLED means the fair price is not switched on yet.

DraftKings prices are DraftKings' own same game parlay pricing, quoted from DraftKings New York (DraftKings runs separate markets in other states); the betslip may differ during a price move, so compare only with a slip taken at the time in meta.pricedAt. A resolved DraftKings leg carries bookSelection: { marketId, selectionId }, DraftKings' own ids; the eventId is DraftKings' numeric event id from /sgp/events?book=draftkings. Every spread, total and player-prop line is confirmed against DraftKings' selection data at pricing time; a line DraftKings has moved since you resolved it is a 422 line-not-echoed or line-mismatch (re-resolve and resend). DraftKings drops legs it will not combine (for example a moneyline together with the same team's spread) and prices the rest; the builder never serves that partial price: it is a 422 bet-failure whose failureCodes carry DraftKings' removal reasons in upper snake case (INCOMPATIBLE_SELECTIONS, REDUNDANT_SELECTION_REMOVED).

DraftKings prices a different set of player props from FanDuel. The categories a player_prop leg can use on DraftKings, per sport: nfl: passing_yards, receiving_yards, and accepted: receptions, rushing_yards, longest_reception, rush_attempts, pass_attempts, pass_completions, interceptions, pass_rush_yards, passing_tds, longest_rush, rush_rec_yards. mlb: accepted: doubles, rbis, runs, hits, walks, hits-runs-rbis, singles, total-bases, stolen-bases, strikeouts, hits-allowed, earned-runs, walks-allowed. nba: points, rebounds, assists, threes_made, steals, blocks, pts_rebs_asts, pts_rebs, pts_asts, rebs_asts. nhl: goals, hockey_points, hockey_assists, shots_on_goal, saves, blocked_shots. ncaaf has no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused before pricing, with the reason in legs[].reason, when it has not. Football and basketball categories use the /props category names (passing_yards, receptions, points, threes_made, pts_rebs_asts; threes is accepted for threes_made), hockey categories use the /props NHL names (hockey_points, hockey_assists, shots_on_goal, saves, blocked_shots, goals), and baseball categories use the builder's MLB names (strikeouts, total-bases). DraftKings player props are priced as two-sided over/unders at the player's main line; the yes-only markets priced are NHL goals (the anytime goal scorer, taken as over 0.5) and NBA, NFL, NHL and MLB N-or-more rungs of a listed over/under category, before the game starts and, on NBA, NFL and NHL, in play (on DraftKings' live ladder): an over leg at N - 0.5 that is not the player's main line prices the N+ rung (over 24.5 is 25+ points, over 89.5 is 90+ receiving yards), with no under side. Other yes-only markets such as anytime touchdown, and NCAAF N-or-more rungs, are refused. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl, ncaaf, mlb, nba and nhl: moneyline, spread and total. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

Hard Rock prices are Hard Rock Bet's own bet-slip price, quoted on its Arizona book (channel ARIZONA_ONLINE): eventId and the ids in bookSelection are the ones the Hard Rock Arizona feed (state az) serves, and a slip in another state can show a different price for the same legs. sgp.decimal is Hard Rock's own parlay price; sgp.american is that decimal expressed in American odds, rounded to a whole number the way the Hard Rock app displays it. Hard Rock game legs price at the main line, except on NHL, where an alternate puck line or total Hard Rock lists also prices, and a team_total leg prices each team's own total (full game, including overtime) at a line Hard Rock lists for that team. On NHL, Hard Rock also prices period legs: the 3-way result of the 1st, 2nd or 3rd period, and a period total or spread at a line it lists. Hard Rock confirms every line in its price response, so no Hard Rock leg is ever priced with lineUnverified. Hard Rock does not combine a moneyline with the same team's spread, or both sides of one total: it drops the leg rather than refusing the slip, and the builder never serves that partial price: the build is a 422 bet-failure with failureCodes INVALID_SELECTION.

Hard Rock prices its own set of player props. The categories a player_prop leg can use on Hard Rock, per sport: nfl: receptions, passing_yards, and accepted: receiving_yards, rushing_yards, passing_tds, interceptions, pass_completions, pass_attempts, rush_rec_yards, touchdowns. mlb: accepted: strikeouts, hits, total-bases, rbis, home-runs, hits-runs-rbis. nhl: accepted: goals, hockey_assists, hockey_points, shots_on_goal, saves, goals_against, power_play_points, blocked_shots. ncaaf and nba have no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused before pricing, with the reason in legs[].reason, when it has not. Football categories use the /props category names (receptions, passing_yards), hockey categories use the /props NHL names (goals, shots_on_goal, hockey_points) plus blocked_shots, and baseball categories use the builder's MLB names (strikeouts, total-bases). A Hard Rock player_prop leg prices at a line Hard Rock lists for that player, including any alternate lines it publishes; a line it does not list is refused with the lines that exist, and a player name that matches more than one player is refused. touchdowns on Hard Rock is the anytime touchdown market, taken as over 0.5, and NHL goals at 0.5 is the anytime goal scorer market. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl, ncaaf, mlb and nba: moneyline, spread and total; nhl: moneyline, spread, total and team_total; moneyline, spread and total also for one period (period P1, P2 or P3). Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

BetRivers and Bally Bet prices are each book's own same game parlay price for exactly the legs sent, quoted from BetRivers Pennsylvania and Bally Bet New Jersey; a slip in another state can show a different price, and prices move, so compare only with a slip taken at the time in meta.pricedAt. Both list and price pregame games only. eventId is the book's numeric event id from /sgp/events?book=betrivers or ?book=ballybet, and a resolved leg carries bookSelection { marketId, selectionId }, the book's own offer and outcome ids. Game legs price at the main line, except on Bally Bet NHL, where an alternate puck line or total Bally Bet lists for same game parlays also prices (BetRivers prices main lines only). Each book confirms every leg's line and status in its price response, so a line it has moved since you resolved it is a 422 line-mismatch (re-resolve and resend). A combination the book will not price (for example both moneylines, or both sides of one total) is a 422 bet-failure with failureCodes COMBINATION_NOT_SUPPORTED; a leg it will not put in a same game parlay is a 422 leg-failure with failureCodes INVALID_OUTCOMES.

BetRivers prices its own set of player props. The categories a player_prop leg can use on BetRivers, per sport: nfl: interceptions, and accepted: passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, pass_attempts, passing_tds, pass_rush_yards, rush_rec_yards. mlb has no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused before pricing, with the reason in legs[].reason, when it has not. Categories use the /props category names (passing_yards, interceptions). A BetRivers player_prop leg prices at the line BetRivers posts for that player and side in the game; another line is refused naming the line that exists, and a side BetRivers does not post is refused. Yes-only and N-or-more markets are not offered as player_prop legs. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl and mlb: moneyline, spread and total. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

Bally Bet prices its own set of player props. The categories a player_prop leg can use on Bally Bet, per sport: nfl: interceptions, and accepted: passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, pass_attempts, passing_tds, pass_rush_yards, rush_rec_yards. ncaaf, mlb, nba and nhl have no player prop categories. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused before pricing, with the reason in legs[].reason, when it has not. Categories use the /props category names (passing_yards, interceptions). A Bally Bet player_prop leg prices at the line Bally Bet posts for that player and side in the game; another line is refused naming the line that exists, and a side Bally Bet does not post is refused. Yes-only and N-or-more markets are not offered as player_prop legs. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl, ncaaf, mlb, nba and nhl: moneyline, spread and total. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

BetMGM prices are BetMGM's own same game parlay price for exactly the legs sent, quoted from BetMGM New Jersey; a slip in another state can show a different price, and prices move, so compare only with a slip taken at the time in meta.pricedAt. BetMGM prices NFL, NBA and NHL, pregame games only. eventId is BetMGM's fixture id from /sgp/events?book=betmgm. Game legs price at the main line only (the spread and total BetMGM lists closest to balanced, the rule /odds uses; when two rungs are equally close, a leg at either rung's line prices, where /odds shows the first listed): an alternate spread or total is refused with the main line. On NFL and NBA, BetMGM's price response repeats every leg's line, status and single price, so a line it has moved since you resolved it is a 422 line-mismatch (re-resolve and resend). NHL is priced through BetMGM's other bet builder: each leg is sent as the option that builder lists for the game, and its price response is one price that names no leg and carries no single, so on NHL legs[].single is null and every leg is in meta.lineUnverifiedLegs; NHL player props are N-or-more rungs (side over at N - 0.5), with no under side. On NHL, a combination the builder will not price (Over with Under of one total) is a 422 bet-failure with failureCodes ZERO_PROBABILITY, or REDUNDANT_LEG when it names the leg it would drop. On NFL and NBA, both sides of one total are a 422 bet-failure with failureCodes ZERO_PROBABILITY; a moneyline with the same team's spread is a 422 bet-failure with failureCodes REDUNDANT_LEG (BetMGM would price the other leg alone, and the builder never serves that partial price); a leg BetMGM's price engine reports no trading data for is a 422 leg-failure with failureCodes NO_TRADING_DATA.

BetMGM prices its own set of player props. The categories a player_prop leg can use on BetMGM, per sport: nfl: receptions, and accepted: passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, passing_tds, pass_completions, rush_attempts, longest_reception, pass_rush_yards, rush_rec_yards. nba: points, and accepted: rebounds, assists, threes_made. nhl: accepted: hockey_points, hockey_assists, shots_on_goal, goals. An accepted category prices when the book posts that market for the player in the game, and the leg is refused before pricing, with the reason in legs[].reason, when it has not. Categories use the /props category names (passing_yards, interceptions). A BetMGM player_prop leg prices at the line BetMGM posts for that player and side in the game; another line is refused naming the line that exists, and a side BetMGM does not post is refused. Yes-only and N-or-more markets are not offered as player_prop legs. A player_prop leg outside these lists is refused with a 422 and a specific reason before pricing. Game legs per sport: nfl, nba and nhl: moneyline, spread and total. Any other game-leg type is refused with a 422 before pricing.

On FanDuel, NBA and WNBA player_prop legs price the player's full-game over/under line. Quarter and alternate lines are not used, so a line that exists only as a quarter or alternate line is refused with the full-game lines that do exist.

A refused player_prop leg names the category you sent and, for a betting-name alias, the props category it stands for. The aliases: anytime_touchdown, anytime-touchdown, anytime_td, anytime-td, atd and touchdown_scorer for touchdowns; first_td and first-td for first_touchdown_scorer.

Batter props on FanDuel are yes/no N-or-more markets, exposed as the over side of N-0.5 (over 0.5 = 1+). They have no under side.

NFL touchdowns and first_touchdown_scorer are yes/no touchdown-scorer markets on FanDuel, exposed the same way: touchdowns over 0.5 is the anytime touchdown scorer, over 1.5 is 2 or more, over 2.5 is 3 or more; first_touchdown_scorer takes over 0.5. They have no under side. NFL passing_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_yards, receptions and passing_tds legs price FanDuel's main line for that player; alternate lines are not used, so a line that exists only on an alternate ladder is refused with the main line that does exist.

Anytime touchdown is priced on FanDuel as touchdowns over 0.5. Hard Rock accepts touchdowns over 0.5 as its anytime touchdown market, not yet verified on a priced parlay. DraftKings does not price it yet: a touchdowns or first_touchdown_scorer leg sent to DraftKings is refused with a 422 before pricing, like every yes-only market except NHL goals (the anytime goal scorer) and, before the game starts, the NBA, NFL, NHL and MLB N-or-more rungs of a listed over/under category.

Builds can be limited per API key per minute, separately from your plan rate limit. Over that limit the call returns 429 { error, code: "SGP_RATE_LIMIT", limit, resetAt } with a Retry-After header, and the refused build does not count against your plan quota. A malformed body, an unsupported or disabled book, and a request refused by your plan rate limit or concurrent request limit do not count toward the per-minute build limit. Every other build does, including one refused afterwards: an invalid eventId (400), a game not found (404), an unresolvable leg (422), a refused parlay (422 with a reasonCode), no price (503 with reasonCode no-price) or SGP_BUSY (503).

A book outside supportedBooks is a 400 with code SGP_BOOK_UNSUPPORTED and supportedBooks, the books the builder prices. A supported book that does not price the requested sport is a 400 with code SGP_BOOK_SPORT_UNSUPPORTED and sports, the sports it does price.

503 means retry later: code SGP_BUSY when pricing capacity is reached (Retry-After: 2), SGP_BOOK_DISABLED when pricing for the requested book is paused (Retry-After: 60; a book whose pricing misbehaves may be paused this way, and a new book may be enabled for selected keys before general availability), and SGP_RATE_LIMIT_UNAVAILABLE when the build limit could not be checked. A 503 with reasonCode no-price (code no-price, Retry-After: 2) means the book produced no usable answer, to the price request or to the read of the game's markets before it: retry later. A 503 without a code is a temporary outage on our side (for example pricing, the rate limit system or subscription verification): back off and retry. The rate limit case carries limit: "system".

A build that reached pricing and returned no price is a 422 or a 503 with the same body; the status says whether to resend. 422 means the book judged the slip and refused it, or its answer did not confirm your legs as sent: the request was valid but cannot be priced as specified, so do not resend the same body unchanged. Its reasonCode is one of duplicate-selection, resp-code, leg-failure, bet-failure, bet-failure-shape, no-sgm-combination, ambiguous-combination, combined-odds-missing, single-missing, single-duplicate, single-odds-missing, runner-odds-missing, runner-odds-duplicate, runner-odds-inconsistent, not-placeable, line-not-echoed, line-mismatch, line-unexpected, line-unverifiable. 503 with reasonCode no-price (and Retry-After: 2) means no usable answer came back at all: the price request failed, timed out or was answered with something other than a price. Retry later. code repeats reasonCode on both (the SDKs expose it as the error's code), so branch on reasonCode first: no-price to retry, unresolved to fix the legs, anything else to change the slip. 502 is not used by this endpoint.

On a refused 422, reasonCode is line-mismatch when the book priced a leg at a different line than requested (re-resolve and resend), bet-failure or leg-failure when the book rejected the parlay or dropped a leg from it (the book's own codes are in failureCodes: FanDuel for example SELECTION_NOT_FOUND, DraftKings INCOMPATIBLE_SELECTIONS or REDUNDANT_SELECTION_REMOVED, Hard Rock INVALID_SELECTION, BetRivers and Bally Bet COMBINATION_NOT_SUPPORTED or INVALID_OUTCOMES, BetMGM ZERO_PROBABILITY, REDUNDANT_LEG or NO_TRADING_DATA), not-placeable when the book is not accepting bets on these legs (for example a suspended market), or another acceptance code when the book's response did not confirm exactly these legs. For line-mismatch and the other line-* codes, legIndex is the leg in your request and lineEchoed is the line the book priced, exactly as it sent it (null when it sent none). message is human-readable prose; match on reasonCode, legIndex, lineEchoed and failureCodes, not on message.

422.description: Legs could not be resolved or the parlay was refused

post.summary: Prices a same game parlay on the book named in book (FanDuel, DraftKings, Hard Rock, BetRivers, Bally Bet and BetMGM): resolves each leg to that book's own selection for one game and returns that book's own correlation-adjusted same game parlay price for exactly those legs, verified leg by leg, not a naive multiplication of the singles.

post.description:
Prices one same game parlay on every same game parlay book at once (FanDuel, DraftKings, Hard Rock, BetRivers, Bally Bet and BetMGM), from our event id, and returns each book's own answer side by side with the best price. Each book's answer is exactly what /sgp/build returns for it.

status says what happened on each book: priced (result is the 200 body), refused (the book refused the parlay: result is its 422 body), unresolved (a leg did not resolve on that book, for example a different main line: result says which and why), busy or no-price (that book produced no usable answer: retry later), timeout (the book had not answered when deadlineMs ran out, or was not reached in time), event-not-listed (the book does not list this game for same game parlays when asked), ambiguous-event (two games match, a doubleheader without -G2, or the book lists this matchup at a different start than this game, or than the other books when the game is under way, so it is a different game), unsupported (the book does not price this sport or one of the legs: reason says which), disabled (that book's pricing is paused) or skipped (fanduel: skip).

The same legs are sent to every book. Books price game legs at their own lines: a spread or total at a number one book does not list (its main line, or on NHL one of the alternates Hard Rock, Bally Bet and, before the game, DraftKings list) is unresolved on that book, with the book's lines in the reason (FanDuel's names only the point); a team_total leg, or a leg with a period, is unsupported on every book except Hard Rock on NHL. best is the highest decimal price among the books that priced. BetRivers and Bally Bet are priced one after the other within the same deadline.

Before a game starts, a book that priced exactly these legs for this game in the last 15 seconds (through /sgp/build or /sgp/compare, for any customer) may be answered from that quote: cached is true, result.meta.cached is true and result.meta.cacheAgeMs is the quote's age when the response was sent; result.meta.pricedAt is still when the book priced it. A cached answer costs no build. Send fresh: true to price every book now. A game that starts within 30 seconds, or is already under way, is always priced fresh.

Every book asked that is not answered from a cached quote counts one build against your per-minute SGP build limit, reserved for the whole comparison before any book is priced; a book that is never asked for a price (not listed, a different game, not reached in time, or a leg that does not resolve) is given back at once while the minute it was counted in is still running. Over the limit the call is a 429 SGP_RATE_LIMIT with unitsNeeded and a Retry-After header. When the comparison needs more builds than your limit allows at all, it is a 429 SGP_COMPARE_TOO_MANY_BOOKS with maxBooks and no Retry-After: ask for at most maxBooks books with books. A comparison counts as one request against your plan rate limit.

MVP and Hall of Fame plans. On a lower plan the call is a 403 with code SGP_TIER_REQUIRED; a 503 with code SGP_FEATURE_DISABLED means comparisons are not switched on yet.

get.description:
Returns betting splits for a sport: handle (money) percent and ticket (bet) percent on each side of the spread, the total and the moneyline of each game, per book, from DraftKings, BetMGM (tickets only) and Circa Sports.

event_id is the eventId /api/v1/{sport}/odds gives the same game ({sport}:{Away}@{Home}-{YYYYMMDD}), and home_team and away_team are the /odds team names, so splits join to odds on event_id. A game not on /odds gets an id built the same way from its scheduled start. Both games of a doubleheader share one event_id, as on /odds.

Each entry in splits carries as_of, when that book's figures were read. The books are read on different schedules, so two books on one game can show different times.

DraftKings figures run until kickoff. After kickoff the last pre-game DraftKings figures stay on the board for up to 4 hours, with the as_of of that last read.

A market a book has not published for a game is absent from that game rather than reported as zero.

meta.books lists the books on the board. meta.as_of is the oldest of their latest reads; a split kept after kickoff carries its own, older as_of. meta.source is a fixed value; read meta.books for the books.

meta.status is "ok" when every book has a recent read, "partial" when one does not (data may then be a subset) and "stale" when no book has one and the last full board, at most 12 hours old, is served instead; meta.age_seconds is then present. meta.partial_reason says which: "book_unavailable" (that book's figures could not be read; it is absent from meta.books), "upstream_limited" (the Circa figures were withheld) or "upstream_paused" (no book could be read and no board from the last 12 hours is available).

BetMGM publishes ticket percentages only, so its entries (book betmgm) carry the bets fields and no handle fields; a percentage absent from any book is not zero.

DraftKings lists splits for only about 50 games of a sport per day, so on a busy slate, such as a full college football Saturday, many games (mostly smaller-conference ones) have no DraftKings split.

get.description:
Returns the same board as /odds reduced to the point spread market.

Kalshi and Polymarket are not in this feed; read them from their v2 source endpoints.

meta.freshness.stale turns true once the board is over 90 seconds old.

meta.market is the market the board was narrowed to (all when none), by the route or by the market parameter.

Query parameters this endpoint does not read are reported in meta.ignored_params rather than rejected; a value the endpoint read but could not apply (an unknown market, a comma list where one value is allowed, a book alias with no valid key) is reported too, with the reason in meta.ignored_reasons.

Unknown book keys inside books are dropped and the applied list is meta.requestedBooks.

home_team and away_team are one canonical string per team across every book for NFL, college football, NBA, NHL, MLB and college basketball: the name as returned is the join key. eventId is {sport}:{away}@{home}-{YYYYMMDD}, built from those names, and is the key the /api/v1/history endpoints use. Soccer and tennis carry each book's own spelling.

/api/v1/normalize maps an outside name (a score feed, a spreadsheet) onto ours; it is not needed for names we return.

home_team_id and away_team_id (homeTeamId and awayTeamId on /api/v1/history/games) are the stable roster id of the team behind each name, the same from every book and spelling. A sample, not a ledger. The source caps each query at 50 rows and gives no cursor, so completeness can never be asserted; above roughly 200 bets a minute the cap binds and the window is undersampled. Do not derive total handle from it.

Every meta key is present on every response shape. On no-data and partial-miss, timestamp, ageSeconds, hash and the bet times are null (there is no data to date) and now is the response clock; never read freshness from a null timestamp.

Every response carries meta.sampling, and sampling.complete is always false. sourceLimit is always present. On an empty response the measured fields windowSeconds and observedNewPerMinute are null; the configured fields pollIntervalMs, configuredWindowMs and configuredMaxEntries are still reported when the feed has run within the last day, and are null only when even that is unknown. observedNewPerMinute is also null on a healthy response until a rate has been measured, which is normal right after a restart.

Legs join to the Stake v2 board on outcome.id and market.id, never on fixture.id, which is a UUID in a different id space. For a fixture-level join use fixture.slug: its numeric prefix appears to be the board fixture id ("46853667-sporting-galatasaray-istanbul" matched board fixture 46853667). Verify that against your own data rather than assuming it.

Each leg carries fixture.tournament { id, name, slug, category } so a wager can be attributed to a competition without matching it to a board first. Observed on every leg sampled. There is no sport field and no tournament-to-sport lookup: category is a grouping (UEFA Champions League gives "International Clubs"), not a sport.

The feed is not filtered by sport, so bets on any sport Stake books can appear, including sports the per-sport board endpoint does not carry (cricket and handball both occur). There is no sport path segment. Any one response is a bounded rolling window of a few minutes, so a low-volume sport may be absent from it.

data[].amount and currency are null when the bettor hid their stake; payout, payoutMultiplier, potentialMultiplier and each leg's odds are nullable too. Skip those rows rather than coercing them to zero.

data[].createdAt and updatedAt pass through in the source's RFC 1123 format; the meta timestamps are ISO 8601.

Bettor identity is never included.

get.description:
Returns a sportsbook's native markets for a sport exactly as the source publishes them: no mapping, no team normalization, no merging. Each entry in data is one raw market blob keyed by the source's own market id.

marketIds narrows data to the listed market ids and prefixes (main,props-* or props-9524; case does not matter). Only those entries are returned, dated in meta.ageSeconds and hashed into the ETag, so a caller of one family keeps its 304s while another family moves. meta.marketIds echoes the filter and meta.marketsFilteredOut counts the entries left out. When the stored board exists but nothing matches, data is empty with meta.cached true and the status and age of the board's primary entries (those outside a family with its own freshness threshold, such as DraftKings game-* and props-*), so it is not mistaken for an outage; if none of those is left (for example only DraftKings game-* and props-* are stored), meta.status is no-data. An entry that is neither an id (letters, digits, - or _) nor a prefix ending in * is a 400. bet365, hardrock, mybookie, stake, thunderpick and underdog ignore marketIds and always return their whole board.

DraftKings nba, nfl, nhl, mlb, ncaab and ncaaf hold main (the league page: game lines), live (the live feed snapshot, when it fits) and one props-<subcategoryId> entry per player-prop subcategory; nba, nfl and ncaaf also hold one game-<subcategoryId> entry per game-market subcategory: 1st half, 1st quarter, team totals, for football alternate spread and alternate total, and for the NBA the game leaders (game-16471 Most Points, game-16472 Most Rebounds, game-16473 Most Assists, game-16474 Most Threes, game-16475 Most Points + Rebounds + Assists: one market per game whose selections are the players, as DraftKings prices them). game-* entries are in the default response, refresh about every 30 seconds, are REST only and are judged against their own 90 second threshold. A default request's meta.status is judged by main and live: a game-* entry kept through a failed refresh does not turn it stale (meta.marketAges shows its age), and when main and live are both gone it reads stale. A marketIds request that includes game-* is judged by those entries too. Each props-* entry is DraftKings' response for that subcategory as received (parsed and re-serialized, not mapped), with its events, markets and selections. props-* entries refresh about every 3 to 5 minutes and are REST only (no draftkings-v2-update message). They are left out unless marketIds asks for them; meta.defaultExcluded then gives their count and the marketIds value that includes them. They are judged fresh against their own 480 second threshold, so they do not turn meta.status stale; meta.marketAges gives each returned entry's age in seconds. When one subcategory's request fails, its previous entry is kept for a cycle; if it reaches its 10 minute lifetime first, a request that includes it reads meta.status partial until the entry is cleared, at the latest on the next cycle.

meta.status is ok, stale, partial or no-data. It flips to stale once ageSeconds passes the book's own freshness threshold, which is set to that book's refresh cadence. Entries in a family with its own threshold (DraftKings game-* and props-*) are judged against that threshold instead, and only when the request asked for them.

Send If-None-Match with the ETag response header, quoted exactly as received (a leading W/ is fine), to receive 304 when nothing changed. The body etag is the same value without quotes, so a bare etag never matches. A 304 on /api/v2 does not count toward your monthly quota; it still counts toward your per-minute limit and appears in your usage log. A key that has used up its monthly quota gets 429 even when the request would have been a 304.

meta.cached is false only when there is no stored board to serve (no-data, and partial-miss on the books that report it). It is not a freshness signal: read meta.ageSeconds and meta.status for that.

For a multi-league sport without league, most books return 400 with a hint to the /leagues index. Books flagged mergeWhenUnspecified instead return a merged board with league null, a leagues index attributing every market to its competition, and meta.merged true; if the merge had to truncate, meta.status is partial, meta.truncated says what was omitted, and meta.omittedIds lists the first 100 omitted market ids, to fetch with marketIds (50 per request) or by passing league.

A few books key data by event rather than by market, so one entry holds a whole game. Each book's sport set, single-league sports and league rules are in the v2Books entries of this manifest.

The SDKs expose one method per book: get<Book>V2 in TypeScript and get_<book>_v2 in Python.

The stake board is the exception to the meta shape above: it serves meta { source, cached, status, timestamp, ageSeconds, hash, now } on every response, with data as an array of fixtures. On no-data and partial-miss, timestamp, ageSeconds and hash are null because there is no board to date, and now is the response clock; never read freshness from a null timestamp.

On stake ice-hockey and basketball, a fixture also carries swish when Stake prices player props for it: Stake's player props (ice hockey: shots on goal, goals, assists, points, hits, plus minus, power play points, blocked shots, and goalie saves once Stake prices them; NBA: points, rebounds, assists, points+assists+rebounds, threes made, double-double, triple-double and first scorer) as { id, status, startTime, players: [{ id, name, position, markets: [{ id, stat: { name }, lines: [{ id, name, line, over, under, balanced, suspended }] }] }] }, over and under in decimal odds. A market lists every line Stake offers: balanced true marks Stake's main line and the others are its alternate lines. Markets with no line are left out, and a game in progress has no swish block because Stake pulls player props once it starts.

propbuilder (Prop Builder) holds one entry per game and market family, family first: game-<gameId> (the game record with home, away, startTime and entries, the ids stored for that game), gfm-<gameId>-<statistic>-<hash> (one game-market group), ou-<gameId>-<statistic>-<hash> (Over/Under lines for one statistic), ss-<gameId>-<statistic>-<hash> (an N+ milestone ladder), ppd-<gameId> (Player Doubles) and h2h-<gameId> (player vs player). marketIds=ou-* returns every Over/Under entry, and game-<gameId>,ou-<gameId>-*,ss-<gameId>-*,gfm-<gameId>-*,ppd-<gameId>,h2h-<gameId> returns one game. gameId is the board's own game id, not the eventId of the /api/v1 endpoints. Odds are decimal, and a market's oddsOverride replaces odds when it is greater than 1. Games are listed until they start, and a market the board suspends or withdraws leaves its entry, as on the board itself. The board sells the game markets (gfm) as parlay legs only, and a leg's price is not the price of a parlay. Several sportsbooks embed this board, and its prices were identical on every site we compared. propbuilder-v2-update pushes changed entries within seconds: load this board on every connect, then apply the messages.

fanatics (Fanatics Sportsbook, not the prediction market) holds one entry per game, keyed by Fanatics' event id: { id, name, startTime, live (true while Fanatics offers in-game betting on it), homeTeam, awayTeam, markets }, teams as { name, abbreviation, nickname }, with every market Fanatics prices for it (moneyline, the full spread and total ladders, team totals, halves and quarters, player milestone props). Each market is { name, bets }, and each bet { id, marketId, name, side, line: { label, value }, status, american, decimal } in Fanatics' own ids: id is the selection id and marketId the market id, so one market of a ladder can hold several Fanatics market ids; side is HOME, AWAY, DRAW, YES or NO where the market has sides; line.label is the line as shown (+3.5, 48, 10+) and line.value its number without the sign (3.5; on correct-score markets read label). Moneyline is two-way in US sports and three-way (with a DRAW side) in soccer; Moneyline 3-Way is the regulation three-way for nba, nhl and ncaaf; Half Time Result is two-way in nfl and ncaaf and three-way in soccer. Only priced selections are listed. A game appears once Fanatics prices it, and while Fanatics prices nothing on it (a suspension) it stays listed with markets [] for up to 30 minutes. Prices are read about every 10 seconds; meta.ageSeconds is the time since the read that last confirmed the game, because the feed carries no change timestamp. nba, nfl, nhl, mlb, ncaaf and ncaab are single-league; soccer is keyed by competition (mls) and merges without league. REST only.

fanaticsmarkets holds one entry per event (the event as Fanatics Markets publishes it, each outcome with its Nadex symbol and probability) and, for every event and market group with a live order book, a books-<eventId>-<group> entry (group: moneyline, spread, over_and_under and so on). books entries are left out unless marketIds asks for them (books-* for all, or marketIds=*). A books entry is { eventId, group, books: { <symbol>: { yes: { bids, asks }, no: { bids, asks }, asOf, live } } }, prices 0 to 1 and sizes in contracts. It is rewritten the moment a book moves on Fanatics Markets; when its group has no book left or the event leaves the board, it is deleted. Over WebSocket the books come on their own event, fanaticsmarkets-books-v2-update, only when you subscribe with books: true next to your fanaticsmarkets sports (v2: { fanaticsmarkets: { nfl: '*', books: true } }); fanaticsmarkets-v2-update keeps carrying the events alone. Each message arrives within about a second of the move and carries books entries (kind books), either whole (replace the entry) or with patch true, carrying only the books that changed (merge them by symbol; null means that book is gone); a deleted entry arrives in removedIds, and about once a minute a group carries ids, the full list of that league's books entries (drop any other entry of that league; other leagues are not affected). To sync: subscribe, hold the messages, load the books entries over REST (?marketIds=books-* with league), then apply what you held. For every message, keep per symbol the book with the later asOf (on a tie, take the message); a null removes the symbol. On a patch for an entry you do not hold, and after every reconnect, load it again over REST. Every entry is also sent whole about every 10 minutes, and once more shortly after a restart on our side. asOf is the time that book last CHANGED on Fanatics Markets, not when we read it: a quiet book keeps an old asOf while still current. live true means the book is held on our open subscription; live false means it is the last state we hold and is not confirmed: our subscription dropped or is reconnecting, or an update arrived for it that we could not apply (it turns true again with the next full book). meta.marketAges gives each entry's age: for a books entry, the seconds since we last confirmed it (at most about 30 while every book in it is live; it keeps growing while one is not); for an event, the seconds since its last refresh (a few minutes). The books response is stale once any books entry is 90 seconds old. The orderbook inside an event entry is a copy taken at the event's refresh, with live as of that refresh (false while our subscription is down, or after an update for it that we could not apply: it is then the last book we hold); read the books entries for live depth.
